what the watch is for

what
a spoken thought reaches my gtd inbox, and the phone rings the watch.
  • why: it’s my gtd tool to remember doing things.
scope
the note stops where the sound reaches the phone.
rule
the watch runs a FOSS OS that talks to my android phone.
  • why: I already have a python runtime on android, so I owe nothing to the annoying standards, like the ones gadgetbridge wants.
    • why: I can do whatever I want.
rule
the work iterates fast and comfortably, on something that reproduces the watch faithfully.
rule
the watch and the phone reach eventual consistency: what one gives the other is kept until taken, and never dropped without saying so.

the stories

what
when I wake up, I start the watch, it connects to my phone, I think about something to be done and speak it into the watch, and it lands in my gtd inbox via the phone.
  • rule: what I speak into the watch reaches my phone as a sound recording.
    • how: once the screen says the phone is linked, the story taps it above its button to start, and again to end; the fake microphone hears a short tone, and the phone must save those very bytes, while the watch’s screen says « saved on the phone ». 
      import asyncio

import companion
from air import spoken_thought, the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "what I speak into the watch reaches my phone as a sound recording"


async def story(work):
    thought = work / "thought.wav"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    spoken_thought(thought)
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        phone = asyncio.create_task(
            companion.receive_one(f"serial:{phone_pty}", work / "inbox"))
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=thought, screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        await written(screen, "phone linked")
        press(work / "wheel.log")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await written(screen, "rec 0:00 / 2:00, tap to end")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        recording = await asyncio.wait_for(phone, 60)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "saved on the phone"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return recording.read_bytes() == thought.read_bytes() and "saved on the phone" in shown
  • rule: what I speak while the phone is away reaches it once linked, one recording at most.
    • how: before the phone links, the story taps twice and the watch keeps the recording; a third tap must be refused; then the phone links and must save those very bytes.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import spoken_thought, the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "what I speak while the phone is away reaches it once linked, one recording at most"


async def story(work):
    thought = work / "thought.wav"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    spoken_thought(thought)
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=thought, screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        await written(screen, "waiting for the phone")
        press(work / "wheel.log")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await written(screen, "rec 0:00 / 2:00, tap to end")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await written(screen, "kept until the phone links")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await written(screen, "one already waiting")
        recording = await asyncio.wait_for(
            companion.receive_one(f"serial:{phone_pty}", work / "inbox"), 60)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "saved on the phone"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return recording.read_bytes() == thought.read_bytes() and "saved on the phone" in shown
rule
a recording whose send breaks reaches the phone at the next link.
  • how: the watch records 20 s of tone; the phone leaves once the screen counts 5 % sent, then links again and must save those very bytes, the screen having said the send stalled.

import asyncio
import contextlib
import wave

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "a recording whose send breaks reaches the phone at the next link"


def long_thought(path):
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as wav:
        wav.setnchannels(1)
        wav.setsampwidth(2)
        wav.setframerate(8000)
        wav.writeframes(bytes(range(256)) * 1250)


async def story(work):
    thought = work / "thought.wav"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    long_thought(thought)
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=thought, screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            receiving = asyncio.create_task(companion.receive_recording(peer))
            await written(screen, "phone linked")
            press(work / "wheel.log")
            tap(taps, 120, 100)
            await written(screen, "rec 0:00 / 2:00, tap to end")
            tap(taps, 120, 100)
            await written(screen, "sending 5 %")
            receiving.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await receiving
        await written(screen, "send stalled, kept")
        recording = await asyncio.wait_for(
            companion.receive_one(f"serial:{phone_pty}", work / "inbox"), 120)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "saved on the phone"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return recording.read_bytes() == thought.read_bytes()
what
later in the day, I check the hour.
  • rule: a glance at the watch shows the right hour.
    • how: once linked, the phone gives its time, a thursday at 07:42; the watch’s screen must then show it, with the date. 
      import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a glance at the watch shows the right hour"
GLANCE = "07:42 Thu 22/10"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.send_time(peer, (2026, 10, 22, 3, 7, 42, 0))
            await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, GLANCE))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return GLANCE in shown
what
when the watch runs low, I notice it before it dies.
  • rule: a watch running low catches my eye.
    • how: the watch starts at 14 %; its screen must say so, its fake motor buzz and its fake speaker ring, once each.

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a watch running low catches my eye"
WARNING = "battery low: 14 %"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=speaker, motor=motor, battery=14)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(speaker, "ring"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    rung = speaker.read_text().splitlines()
    buzzed = motor.read_text().splitlines() if motor.exists() else []
    return WARNING in shown and rung == ["ring"] and buzzed == ["buzz"]
what
later, I get a recall; it comes from my phone and rings in the watch.
  • rule: a recall my phone sends rings the watch.
    • how: once the voice is sent, the phone writes a recall’s text, priority 4, sent on the 22/10 at 07:40; the watch, which knows no date, must show that text after that date and hour, its fake speaker must have rung once and its fake motor buzzed once. 
      import asyncio

import companion
from air import spoken_thought, the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "a recall my phone sends rings the watch"
RECALL = "call the dentist"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)
SHOWN = "22/10 07:40 call the dentist"


async def story(work):
    thought = work / "thought.wav"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    spoken_thought(thought)
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=thought, screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=speaker, motor=motor, wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            recording = asyncio.create_task(companion.receive_recording(peer))
            await written(screen, "phone linked")
            press(work / "wheel.log")
            tap(taps, 120, 100)
            await written(screen, "rec 0:00 / 2:00, tap to end")
            tap(taps, 120, 100)
            await asyncio.wait_for(recording, 60)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, RECALL, priority=4, when=SENT)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(speaker, "ring"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    rung = speaker.read_text().splitlines() if speaker.exists() else []
    buzzed = motor.read_text().splitlines() if motor.exists() else []
    # the press and the two taps tick; only the buzz is the recall's
    return SHOWN in shown and rung == ["ring"] and [b for b in buzzed if b != "tick"] == ["buzz"]
  • rule: a recall from a noisy sender shows without a sound.
    • how: once linked, the phone writes a recall, priority 2, then another, priority 4; the watch’s screen must show both, its fake motor have buzzed and its fake speaker rung only once, for the second.

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a recall from a noisy sender shows without a sound"
QUIET = "a new follower"
LOUD = "call the dentist"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=speaker, motor=motor)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.send_recall(peer, QUIET, priority=2, when=SENT)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, LOUD, priority=4, when=SENT)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(speaker, "ring"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    rung = speaker.read_text().splitlines()
    buzzed = motor.read_text().splitlines()
    both = "22/10 07:40 " + QUIET in shown and "22/10 07:40 " + LOUD in shown
    return both and rung == ["ring"] and buzzed == ["buzz"]
rule
recalls I have not looked at yet stand out, until my next tap or press.
  • why: « new notif watching phone highlighted, like bold or something »
  • how: once linked, the phone writes two recalls; both must stand out, then a tap must make them plain; then a third, which a press of the wheel must make plain.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "recalls I have not looked at yet stand out, until my next tap or press"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)
MARKS = ["fresh 22/10 07:40 one", "fresh 22/10 07:40 two", "seen", "fresh 22/10 07:40 three", "seen"]


async def marked(fresh, count):
    for _ in range(200):
        if len(fresh.read_text().splitlines()) >= count:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    fresh = work / "screen.log.fresh"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log", wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "one", priority=2, when=SENT)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "two", priority=2, when=SENT)
            await written(screen, "22/10 07:40 two")
            tap(work / "taps.log", 120, 100)
            await written(fresh, "seen")
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "three", priority=2, when=SENT)
            await written(screen, "22/10 07:40 three")
            press(work / "wheel.log")
            await marked(fresh, len(MARKS))
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(fresh, "seen"))
    marks = fresh.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  fresh: {' / '.join(marks)}")
    return marks == MARKS
rule
a recall’s color tells its priority.
  • how: once linked, the phone writes three recalls, priority 2, 3 and 4; the watch must draw them cyan, yellow and red.

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a recall's color tells its priority"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            for priority in (2, 3, 4):
                await companion.send_recall(peer, f"priority {priority}", priority=priority, when=SENT)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "22/10 07:40 priority 4"))
    tints = (work / "screen.log.tints").read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  tints: {' / '.join(tints)}")
    return tints == ["cyan", "yellow", "red"]
rule
a phone that leaves halfway can link again.
  • how: the phone links and leaves before saying it is ready; it must then find the watch again and give it a recall the screen shows.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a phone that leaves halfway can link again"
SHOWN = "22/10 07:40 linked again"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}"):
            pass
        async with asyncio.timeout(20):
            async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
                await companion.send_recall(peer, "linked again", priority=2,
                                            when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40))
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, SHOWN))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return SHOWN in shown
what
a notification comes to my phone; I read it on the watch, without taking the phone out.
  • rule: a notification posted on the linked phone shows whole on the watch.
    • how: once linked, the phone gets a notification from Signal, titled « Alice », saying « on my way, I will be there in ten minutes », on the 22/10 at 07:40; the watch’s screen must show it whole, cut at the spaces into rows that fit its 30 columns, those rows alone in the recall color.
    • how: then « Bob » says « see you »; each recall opens on its own rule, so the two come apart.

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a notification posted on the linked phone shows whole on the watch"
ROWS = ["22/10 07:40 Signal: Alice: on", "my way, I will be there in ten", "minutes"]
NEXT = ["22/10 07:41 Signal: Bob: see", "you"]
RULE = "-" * 30


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.notify(peer, "Signal", "Alice", "on my way, I will be there in ten minutes",
                                   when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40))
            await companion.notify(peer, "Signal", "Bob", "see you", when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 41))
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, NEXT[-1]))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    recalled = (work / "screen.log.recalls").read_text().splitlines()
    return (any(shown[at:at + len(ROWS)] == ROWS for at in range(len(shown)))
            and recalled == [RULE] + ROWS + [RULE] + NEXT)
rule
an ntfy post shows short: its topic and message, once, links as hosts, times as hh:mm.
  • how: once linked, the phone gets an ntfy notification titled « 192.168.2.14:9705/n », saying « A@memories (12s) », on the 22/10 at 07:40; the watch’s screen must show ntfy’s icon, then « n: A@memories (12s) ».
  • how: its twin, « 07:40:A@memories (12s) », the same minute, must not show.
  • how: then « 🚨📷 oxenhead » says « seen http://192.168.2.14:9917/explore?x=1 at 2026-10-22 05:46:59.123 »; it must show as « oxenhead: seen 192.168.2.14:9917 at 05:46 ».

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "an ntfy post shows short: its topic and message, once, links as hosts, times as hh:mm"
RULE = "-" * 30
ROWS = [RULE, "\x0e\x0f22/10 07:40 n: A@memories", "  (12s)",
        RULE, "\x0e\x0f22/10 07:41 oxenhead: seen", "  192.168.2.14:9917 at 05:46"]


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.notify(peer, "ntfy", "192.168.2.14:9705/n", "A@memories (12s)",
                                   when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40))
            await companion.notify(peer, "ntfy", "192.168.2.14:9705/n", "07:40:A@memories (12s)",
                                   when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40))
            await companion.notify(peer, "ntfy", "🚨📷 oxenhead",
                                   "seen http://192.168.2.14:9917/explore?x=1 at 2026-10-22 05:46:59.123",
                                   when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 41))
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, ROWS[-1]))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return (work / "screen.log.recalls").read_text().splitlines() == ROWS
rule
a notification in french shows its accents.
  • how: once linked, the phone gets an ntfy notification titled « 192.168.2.14:9705/n », saying « été, à, ç, œ », on the 22/10 at 07:40; the watch’s screen must show « n: été, à, ç, oe », beside ntfy’s icon.
  • scope: the fake screen writes the text as it comes; the glyphs the real screen draws are not checked here.

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a notification in french shows its accents"
SHOWN = ["\x0e\x0f22/10 07:40 n: été, à, ç,", "  oe"]


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.notify(peer, "ntfy", "192.168.2.14:9705/n", "été, à, ç, œ",
                                   when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40))
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, SHOWN[-1]))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return any(shown[at:at + len(SHOWN)] == SHOWN for at in range(len(shown)))
rule
a known app’s icon stands doubled at the left of its line, over two rows, the stamp and text in one column beside it.
  • why: « icons shluld be bigger », « taller », « also alçgned w_th text »
  • how: once linked, the phone notifies « Alice: on my way » from a call, an SMS app, WhatsApp, a mail, a calendar and ntfy, on the 22/10 at 07:40; each must show as its icon, then « 22/10 07:40 Alice: on my », and below, beside the icon, « way ».
  • scope: the fake screen writes the codes as they come; icons-preview.py draws what the real screen draws, for an eye to check.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "a known app's icon stands doubled at the left of its line, over two rows, the stamp and text in one column beside it"
ICONS = ("\x01\x02", "\x03\x04", "\x05\x06", "\x07\x08", "\x10\x11", "\x0e\x0f")
# each app as the android listener names it: its name, package and category
APPS = (("Phone", "com.google.android.dialer", "call"),
        ("Messages", "com.google.android.apps.messaging", "msg"),
        ("WhatsApp", "com.whatsapp", "msg"),
        ("K-9 Mail", "com.fsck.k9", "email"),
        ("Calendar", "org.fossify.calendar", "event"),
        ("ntfy", "io.heckel.ntfy", None))
FIRST = "22/10 07:40 Alice: on my"
NEXT = "  way"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            for app, package, category in APPS:
                await companion.notify(peer, app, "Alice", "on my way", when=(2026, 10, 22, 7, 40),
                                       package=package, category=category)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, ICONS[-1] + FIRST))
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return all(any(shown[at:at + 2] == [icon + FIRST, NEXT] for at in range(len(shown))) for icon in ICONS)
what
at night, I need light to find my way, and the watch is on my wrist.
  • rule: holding the wheel, then a tap on the pad’s left, lights the watch as a torch, and a tap puts it out, read-only.
    • how: the watch starts dark; the story holds the wheel, and the actions pad must open; it taps its left, and the screen must say « torch on »; then it taps once, and the screen must say « torch off », after the torch came on; a tap a second later must record nothing.

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, hold, written

PROMISE = "holding the wheel, then a tap on the pad's left, lights the watch as a torch, and a tap puts it out, read-only"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  dark=True, wheel=wheel)
        hold(wheel)
        await written(work / "screen.log.media", "pad actions")
        tap(taps, 40, 100)
        await written(screen, "torch on")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await written(screen, "torch off")
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "torch off"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    recorded = any(line.startswith("rec ") for line in shown)
    return shown.index("torch on") < shown.index("torch off") and not recorded
what
reading or showing something on the watch, 5 s of light are too short.
  • rule: a tap on the actions pad’s top row turns it to its second page, and a tap on « stay lit » there keeps the screen lit a minute after each wake, for ten minutes; a second one ends it.
    • why: « add an option to temporarily change the screen wake time »
    • how: the story holds the wheel, and the actions pad must open; it taps the top row, and the second page must open; it taps its middle, and the screen must say « lit 1 min for 10 min » and stay lit 7 s; it does it all again, and the screen must say « dark after 5 s again » and darken; no tap may record.
    • scope: it checks the screen outlasts the 5 s, not the full minute nor the ten.

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, hold, written

PROMISE = "a tap on the actions pad's top row turns it to its second page, and a tap on « stay lit » there keeps the screen lit past the 5 s; a second one ends it"


async def nth(path, line, count):
    for _ in range(200):
        if path.exists() and path.read_text().splitlines().count(line) >= count:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    raise TimeoutError(f"{path.name} never said {line} {count} times")


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    pads = work / "screen.log.media"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    dark = work / "screen.log.dark"

    def darks():
        return dark.read_text().splitlines().count("dark") if dark.exists() else 0

    async def turn(count, said):
        hold(wheel)
        await nth(pads, "pad actions", count)
        tap(taps, 120, 5)
        await nth(pads, "pad more", count)
        tap(taps, 120, 150)
        await written(screen, said)
        await nth(pads, "pad off", count)

    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  dark=True, wheel=wheel)
        await turn(1, "lit 1 min for 10 min")
        before = darks()
        await asyncio.sleep(7)
        stayed = darks() == before
        await turn(2, "dark after 5 s again")
        await nth(dark, "dark", before + 1)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "dark after 5 s again"))
    shown = screen.read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"  screen: {' / '.join(shown)}, stayed lit: {stayed}")
    recorded = any(line.startswith("rec ") for line in shown)
    ordered = shown.index("lit 1 min for 10 min") < shown.index("dark after 5 s again")
    return ordered and stayed and not recorded
what
a picture shared on the phone, I want to see on my wrist.
  • rule: a picture the phone writes on PICTURE fills the band between the hour and the bar, each half-row where it belongs, stays lit past the 5 s, and the wheel puts the lines back.
    • why: « it must also show between the hour and the bar at the bottom; those are supposed static »
    • why: « it must prevent going to sleep until I press the wheel »
    • how: the story links as the phone, writes a 240x208 picture whose every pixel tells its place, and the screen must say « picture on » and draw all 416 half-rows, each starting with its own pixel; it waits 6 s, and the screen must not have darkened; then it presses the wheel, and the screen must say « picture off ».

import asyncio
import struct

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, press, written

PROMISE = "a picture the phone writes on PICTURE fills the band between the hour and the bar, each half-row where it belongs, stays lit past the 5 s, and the wheel puts the lines back"


def pixels():
    return b"".join(struct.pack(">H", y * 256 + x) for y in range(208) for x in range(240))


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log", wheel=wheel)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.send_picture(peer, pixels())
        await written(screen, "picture on")
        await written(work / "screen.log.picture", "207,1,cf78")
        await asyncio.sleep(6)
        darkened = (work / "screen.log.dark").exists()
        press(wheel)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "picture off"))
    drawn = (work / "screen.log.picture").read_text().splitlines()
    wanted = ["%d,%d,%04x" % (y, half, y * 256 + half * 120) for y in range(208) for half in (0, 1)]
    print(f"  half-rows drawn: {len(drawn)}, misplaced: {len(set(wanted) - set(drawn))}, dark: {darkened}")
    return sorted(drawn) == sorted(wanted) and not darkened
what
when the watch starts, it lights, and a stray touch must not record.

a script sent to a watch out of reach says so in one line, naming the bar’s « W » to tap.
  • how: the story sends a script toward a port nobody listens on; it must end failed, its one line naming the « W ».

import asyncio
import os
import socket

from air import ROOT

PROMISE = "a script sent to a watch out of reach says so in one line, naming the bar's « W » to tap"


async def story(work):
    with socket.socket() as probe:
        probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = probe.getsockname()[1]
    sent = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        str(ROOT / "over-wifi.sh"), "true",
        env={**os.environ, "TWATCH_HOST": "127.0.0.1", "TWATCH_PORT": str(port)},
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT)
    said = (await sent.communicate())[0].decode().splitlines()
    print(f"  said: {' / '.join(said)}")
    return sent.returncode != 0 and len(said) == 1 and "the watch's bar so « W » joins" in said[0]
what
before i speak into the watch, i glance at the bar to know whether the phone is linked.
  • rule: the bar’s « B » tells by its color whether the phone is linked.
    • how: the watch starts unlinked, its « B » yellow; once the phone links and says it is ready, the « B » must turn green, and yellow again once the phone leaves.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, written

PROMISE = "the bar's « B » tells by its color whether the phone is linked"


def tints(bar):
    return [line for line in bar.read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith("B ")]


async def left(bar):
    for _ in range(200):
        if tints(bar)[-1:] == ["B yellow"]:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)


async def story(work):
    bar = work / "screen.log.bar"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        await written(bar, "B yellow")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            ready = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(companion.READY, companion.SERVICE)[0]
            await peer.write_value(ready, b"phone", with_response=True)
            await written(bar, "B green")
        await left(bar)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(bar, "B green"))
    shown = tints(bar)
    print(f"  bar: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return shown == ["B yellow", "B green", "B yellow"]
what

    • why: « a way to cuange brightness »
    • why: « control with q slider instead in the 1.5s :enu? »

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, hold, written

async def story(work):

    taps = work / "taps.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):

        await written(light, "light 25%")

        await written(work / "motor.log", "tick")
        for x, level in ((143, "60%"), (0, "2%")):

            await written(light, "light " + level)
        tap(taps, 239, 30)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(light, "light 100%"))

    print(f"  light: {' / '.join(shown)}")

what
when the watch crashes, I want it back, and to learn why from the phone.
  • rule: a crash restarts the watch, and its traceback reaches the phone at the next link, then is gone from the watch.
    • why: « log excep(ions somewhere boot resistant and at next lçnk send to phone and purge »
    • how: the story feeds the fake touch a tap it cannot read, which raises; the watch must end, its traceback kept; started again, once the phone links, the phone must hear the ValueError and the watch’s file must be gone.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, written

PROMISE = "a crash restarts the watch, and its traceback reaches the phone at the next link, then is gone from the watch"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    errors = work / "errors.log"
    fakes = dict(mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps, speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                 motor=work / "motor.log")
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, **fakes)
        await written(screen, "waiting for the phone")
        taps.write_text("boom,\n")
        ended = await asyncio.wait_for(watch.wait(), 10)
        kept = errors.read_text() if errors.exists() else ""
        taps.write_text("")
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, **fakes)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            heard = await companion.receive_errors(peer, "ValueError")
            await written(screen, "errors sent to the phone")
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "errors sent to the phone"))
    print(f"  ended: {ended}, kept: {len(kept)} bytes, heard: {heard[-1]}, left: {errors.exists()}")
    return ended != 0 and "ValueError" in kept and not errors.exists()
what
I read the watch’s charge from afar without touching it.

    • why: « this must be captured in the poc app itself, not via the desktop »; a read over the REPL halts the watch’s main.py.
    • how: the story links a phone to a watch at 80 %; the phone must hear a « charge 80 % » line on CHARGE, the watch’s errors staying on ERRORS.
      • why: « 2 »: a charge is no error, so it has its own channel and the phone logs it as « watch charge ».

        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",

        await written(screen, "waiting for the phone")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            heard = await companion.receive_charge(peer, "charge")
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "waiting for the phone"))

with two phones around, I choose on the watch the one it links with.
  • rule: the actions pad’s middle column steps through « any phone » and the phones seen, and a phone other than the chosen one is dropped once it says its name.
    • why: « can we in a menu of watch decide whar phàneto use ? »
    • how: a phone named « phone » links and leaves; the story holds the wheel and taps the middle column, which must then read « phone »; a phone named « other » must then be refused.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, hold, written

PROMISE = "the actions pad's middle column steps through « any phone » and the phones seen, and a phone other than the chosen one is dropped once it says its name"


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=motor, wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.say_ready(peer, "phone")

        hold(work / "wheel.log")

            await asyncio.wait_for(peer.gone, 10)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "other refused, phone chosen"))

what
while I use the watch, it must not go dark under my finger.
  • rule: every tap or press restarts the screen’s 5 s before it darkens.
    • why: « every interaction with the watch must reset the 5s timer »
    • how: the story presses the wheel, then taps the hour row every 2 s, four times, 8 s in all; each tap must tick the motor, the screen still lit; 7 s after the last, it must be dark.

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "every tap or press restarts the screen's 5 s before it darkens"
EVERY_S = 2
TAPS = 4
DARK_S = 7


async def story(work):
    light = work / "screen.log.light"
    dark = work / "screen.log.dark"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=taps, speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=motor, wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        await written(light, "light 25%")
        press(work / "wheel.log")
        for _ in range(TAPS):
            await asyncio.sleep(EVERY_S)
            tap(taps, 120, 8)
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
        ticked = motor.read_text().splitlines().count("tick") - 1
        darkened_early = dark.exists()
        await asyncio.sleep(DARK_S)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(light, "light 25%"))
        darkened = dark.exists()
    print(f"  ticks: {ticked}, dark early: {darkened_early}, dark after: {darkened}")
    return ticked == TAPS and not darkened_early and darkened
rule
a tap on the dark screen is answered within 0.3 s.
  • why: « tap to wake is not react_ve enough »
  • how: the story waits for the screen to darken, then taps; the fake motor must tick within 0.3 s.

import asyncio
import time

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, written

PROMISE = "a tap on the dark screen is answered within 0.3 s"
WITHIN_S = 0.3


def ticks(motor):
    return motor.read_text().splitlines().count("tick") if motor.exists() else 0


async def story(work):
    dark = work / "screen.log.dark"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=taps, speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=motor)
        while not dark.exists():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
        tapped = time.monotonic()
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        while ticks(motor) == 0 and time.monotonic() - tapped < 3:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        answered = time.monotonic() - tapped
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(motor, "tick"))
    print(f"  answered in {answered:.2f} s")
    return answered < WITHIN_S
rule
a tap on the dark screen wakes it even if the finger lifted before the watch looked.
  • why: « a lot of taps just don’t wake the watch »
  • how: the story waits for the screen to darken, then taps one the panel no longer holds; light.log must then say « wake tap ».

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, lose

PROMISE = "a tap on the dark screen wakes it even if the finger lifted before the watch looked"


def woken(trace):
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    return any(line.split()[1:3] == ["wake", "tap"] for line in kept)


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    dark = work / "screen.log.dark"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=taps, speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log")
        while not dark.exists():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        lose(taps)
        for _ in range(30):
            if woken(trace):
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        watch.terminate()
        await watch.wait()
    print(f"  woken: {woken(trace)}")
    return woken(trace)
rule
a wheel press on the dark screen lights it within 0.3 s.
  • why: « wheel wakes after like 4s »
  • how: the story waits for the screen to darken, presses the wheel mid-nap; light.log must say « wake wheel » within 0.3 s.

import asyncio
import time

from air import the_air, start_watch, press

PROMISE = "a wheel press on the dark screen lights it within 0.3 s"
WITHIN_S = 0.3


def woken(trace):
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    return any(line.split()[1:3] == ["wake", "wheel"] for line in kept)


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    dark = work / "screen.log.dark"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log", wheel=wheel)
        while not dark.exists():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
        pressed = time.monotonic()
        press(wheel)
        while not woken(trace) and time.monotonic() - pressed < 3:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        answered = time.monotonic() - pressed
        watch.terminate()
        await watch.wait()
    print(f"  answered in {answered:.2f} s")
    return answered < WITHIN_S
rule
a press or a tap on the dark screen is felt before the screen wakes.
  • why: « shpuld vibrate when gettçnf the tap/press, not when lighton the screen »
  • how: the fake motor writes into light.log itself, so its « tick » and the screen’s « wake » stand in the order they came; a dark press, then a dark tap, must each put the tick first.

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, press, tap

PROMISE = "a press or a tap on the dark screen is felt before the screen wakes"


def lines(trace):
    return trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []


async def dark_again(trace, after):
    while not any(line.split()[1:2] == ["dark"] for line in lines(trace)[after:]):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return len(lines(trace))


async def woken(trace, after, why):
    for _ in range(30):
        kept = lines(trace)[after:]
        for at, line in enumerate(kept):
            if line.split()[1:3] == ["wake", why]:
                return "tick" in kept[:at]
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return False


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=taps, speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=trace, wheel=wheel)
        seen = await dark_again(trace, 0)
        press(wheel)
        pressed = await woken(trace, seen, "wheel")
        seen = await dark_again(trace, seen)
        tap(taps, 120, 100)
        tapped = await woken(trace, seen, "tap")
        watch.terminate()
        await watch.wait()
    print(f"  felt first: press {pressed}, tap {tapped}")
    return pressed and tapped
rule
each dark and wake of the screen is kept, with what caused it and the ms since the one before, in a small file on the flash.
  • why: « never work aroud, always fix. If not clear, add logs to improve knowledge »
  • how: the story starts the watch dark; its first line, « waiting for the phone », lights it, so the fake screen’s light.log must say « wake line ».
  • why: « i thçnk it happens after some time of inacrivity »: the log must say what touched the panel.
  • how: a wake also keeps what it shows: lines, torch, picture or the pad’s name, how many lines are kept and the last one, so its line must end « : lines N waiting for the phone ».
    • why: the blank’s start is not remembered; a wake that showed lines tells a lost panel from an empty one.
  • how: the main loop also writes « alive » there at its first turn, then every 5 min, so a hang shows as a gap; the story sees the first one, the 5 min stay untested, no story waiting them.
    • why: at 14:01 the log went silent until the RST, and whether main.py hung could not be told.

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "each dark and wake of the screen is kept, with what caused it and the ms since the one before, in a small file on the flash"


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log", dark=True)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "waiting for the phone"))
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    print(f"  kept: {' / '.join(kept)}")
    return (any(line.split()[1:3] == ["wake", "line"] and ": lines " in line
                and line.endswith("waiting for the phone") for line in kept)
            and any(line.split()[1:2] == ["alive"] for line in kept))
rule
each « alive » also says how long the watch stayed awake since the one before, its loop’s turns, and how many times a dark nap’s slice woke it.
  • why: « Time the dark watch’s own wakes, its nap slices and the link’s radio, and cut the biggest »
  • why: overnight, dark and untouched, the watch lost 1.45 %/h with no wake logged; what wakes it is unknown.
  • how: the story sees the first « alive » read « alive awake N turns N slices N ».

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "each alive also says how long the watch stayed awake since the one before, its loop's turns, and how many times a dark nap's slice woke it"


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log", dark=True)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "waiting for the phone"))
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    alive = [line.split()[1:] for line in kept if line.split()[1:2] == ["alive"]]
    print(f"  alive: {alive}")
    return any(len(words) >= 7 and words[1:7:2] == ["awake", "turns", "slices"]
               and all(word.isdigit() for word in words[2:7:2])
               for words in alive)
rule
each « alive » also says how long the chip light-slept since the one before, and how many light sleeps it made and refused.
  • why: « so 4 is a measure, and 2 is an improvement ? Why make a false choice then, it’s obviously 4 AND 2 »
  • how: the story sees an « alive » end « slept N sleeps N refused N ».
  • scope: the fake chip sleeps never; the firmware’s own counting is reached on the watch only.

PROMISE = "each alive also says how long the chip light-slept since the one before, and how many light sleeps it made and refused"


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",

what
while a new firmware crawls to the watch over its wifi, I glance at the watch to know how far it is.
  • rule: while a firmware is sent, the watch and the send’s log show each piece landed, in percent, and the time left at the pace so far.
    • why: « also, durin that time, can the watch show the progress as well ? », then « and an ETA ? »
    • how: the story lands four small pieces on the fake watch; each but the last must show « firmware N %, T left », the last « firmware 100 % », the same lines printed, and the pieces whole in app.bin.

import asyncio
import os
import re

from air import ROOT

PROMISE = "while a firmware is sent, the watch and the send's log show each piece landed, in percent, and the time left at the pace so far"
PIECES = 4
LEFT = re.compile(r"firmware \d+ %, (\d+ h \d\d|\d+ min|\d+ s) left")


async def story(work):
    script = f"import pieces\npieces.start({PIECES})\n"
    for n in range(PIECES):
        script += f"open('app.part', 'wb').write(b'{n}' * 10)\npieces.add()\n"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    sent = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        os.environ["TWATCH_MICROPYTHON"], "-c", script, cwd=work,
        env={**os.environ, "MICROPYPATH": f"{ROOT / 'watch'}:{ROOT / 'fake'}",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN": str(screen), "TWATCH_FAKE_DARK": "1",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_ERRORS": str(work / "errors.log"), "TWATCH_FAKE_PHONE": str(work / "phone.txt")},
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT)
    said = (await sent.communicate())[0].decode().splitlines()
    shown = [line for line in screen.read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith("firmware")] if screen.exists() else []
    whole = (work / "app.bin").read_bytes() if (work / "app.bin").exists() else b""
    print(f"  shown: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    print(f"  said: {' / '.join(said)}")
    return (len(shown) == PIECES and all(LEFT.fullmatch(line) for line in shown[:-1])
            and shown[-1] == "firmware 100 %" and said == shown
            and whole == b"".join(str(n).encode() * 10 for n in range(PIECES)))
what
after a flash over usb, the watch runs again as before it.
  • rule: after a flash’s erase, one script puts back every file the watch runs, main.py among them, then restarts it.
    • why: « a bad tool is fixed »: the erase took every file, and the note’s flash ended on « press RST ».
    • how: the story runs the restore against an empty fake watch, a fake mpremote standing for the cable; the files must land there whole, main.py among them, and a reset come last; « every file » is main.py and boot.py and every module of the note they import, then those import, and so on.

import asyncio
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

from air import ROOT

PROMISE = "after a flash's erase, one script puts back every file the watch runs, main.py among them, then restarts it"
MPREMOTE = """
import os, shutil, sys
os.chdir(os.environ["TWATCH_FAKE_FLASH"])
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:1] == ["connect"]:
    args = args[2:]
if args[:1] == ["resume"]:
    args = args[1:]
place = {}
commands = [[]]
for arg in args:
    if arg == "+":
        commands.append([])
    else:
        commands[-1].append(arg)
for command in commands:
    if command[0] == "exec":
        exec(command[1], place)
    elif command[0] == "cp":
        shutil.copy(command[1], command[2].lstrip(":"))
    elif command[0] == "run":
        exec(open(command[1]).read(), place)
    with open(os.environ["TWATCH_FAKE_CABLE"], "a") as cable:
        cable.write(command[0] + "\\n")
"""


async def story(work):
    tree, bin, flash, lcd = work / "tree", work / "bin", work / "flash", work / "st7789"
    for place in (bin, flash, lcd / "lib", lcd / "romfonts"):
        place.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "watch", tree / "watch")
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "device", tree / "device")
    for script in ("deploy-watch.sh", "restore-watch.sh"):
        if (ROOT / script).exists():
            shutil.copy(ROOT / script, tree / script)
    (lcd / "lib" / "st7789py.py").write_text("WIDTH = 240\n")
    (lcd / "romfonts" / "vga2_8x16.py").write_text("HEIGHT = 16\n")
    (bin / "nix-shell").write_text('#!/bin/sh\nexec bash "$@"\n')
    (bin / "mpremote").write_text(f"#!{sys.executable}\n{MPREMOTE}")
    for fake in ("nix-shell", "mpremote"):
        (bin / fake).chmod(0o755)
    cable = work / "cable.log"
    restored = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        "bash", str(tree / "restore-watch.sh"), "/dev/null",
        env={**os.environ, "PATH": f"{bin}:{os.environ['PATH']}", "ST7789PY": str(lcd),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_FLASH": str(flash), "TWATCH_FAKE_CABLE": str(cable)},
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT)
    said = (await restored.communicate())[0].decode().splitlines()
    places = [tree / "watch", tree / "device", lcd / "lib", lcd / "romfonts"]
    wanted, todo = {}, ["boot", "main"]
    while todo:
        name = todo.pop()
        file = next((place / f"{name}.py" for place in places if (place / f"{name}.py").exists()), None)
        if name in wanted or file is None:
            continue
        wanted[name] = file
        text = file.read_text()
        todo += re.findall(r"^\s*from\s+(\w+)", text, re.M)
        for names in re.findall(r"^\s*import\s+([\w, ]+)", text, re.M):
            todo += [part.split()[0] for part in names.split(",") if part.strip()]
    missing = sorted(file.name for file in wanted.values()
                     if not (flash / file.name).exists() or (flash / file.name).read_bytes() != file.read_bytes())
    steps = cable.read_text().split() if cable.exists() else []
    print(f"  said: {' / '.join(said[-3:])}")
    print(f"  run by the watch: {len(wanted)}, missing: {missing}, last step: {steps[-1:]}")
    return restored.returncode == 0 and "main" in wanted and not missing and steps[-1:] == ["reset"]
rule
each write the phone makes to the watch is kept in the same file, named and counted.
  • why: « never work aroud, always fix. If not clear, add logs to improve knowledge »
  • why: from 14:04 to 14:22 the watch left the phone’s writes unanswered, and nothing told what reached it.
  • how: a phone links, says its name and sends a recall; light.log must then hold a « heard » line naming « ready » and one naming « recall ».

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, written

PROMISE = "each write the phone makes to the watch is kept in the same file, named and counted"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.say_ready(peer, "phone")
            await written(screen, "phone linked")
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "call the dentist", priority=2, when=SENT)
            await written(screen, "22/10 07:40 call the dentist")
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "waiting for the phone"))
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    heard = [line.split()[2:] for line in kept if line.split()[1:2] == ["heard"]]
    print(f"  heard: {' / '.join(' '.join(words) for words in heard)}")
    return any("ready" in words for words in heard) and any("recall" in words for words in heard)
rule
the watch keeps its charge in the same file, percent and mV, at its start and then each hour.
  • why: « focus on preserving the battery the longer possible »: a saving’s worth is the drop per hour.
  • how: the fake battery says 80 % and 3900 mV, so light.log must hold « charge 80 3900 »; the hour stays untested.

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "the watch keeps its charge in the same file, percent and mV, at its start and then each hour"


async def story(work):
    trace = work / "light.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=work / "taps.log",
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log")
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "waiting for the phone"))
    kept = trace.read_text().splitlines() if trace.exists() else []
    charges = [line.split()[2:] for line in kept if line.split()[1:2] == ["charge"]]
    print(f"  charges: {' / '.join(' '.join(words) for words in charges)}")
    return any(words[:2] == ["80", "3900"] for words in charges)
what
on the move, I touch the watch without looking at it.
  • rule: each tap and wheel press the watch takes answers with a short tick of its motor.
    • why: « haptic feedback »
    • how: the story presses the wheel, then taps the hour row; the fake motor must have ticked twice.

import asyncio

from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "each tap and wheel press the watch takes answers with a short tick of its motor"


async def ticked(motor, count):
    for _ in range(200):
        if motor.exists() and len(motor.read_text().splitlines()) >= count:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)


async def story(work):
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    light = work / "screen.log.light"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, _):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=motor, wheel=work / "wheel.log")
        await written(light, "light 25%")
        press(work / "wheel.log")
        await ticked(motor, 1)
        tap(work / "taps.log", 120, 8)
        await ticked(motor, 2)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(light, "light 25%"))
    shown = motor.read_text().splitlines() if motor.exists() else []
    print(f"  motor: {' / '.join(shown)}")
    return shown == ["tick", "tick"]
what
my watch is somewhere in the flat; I make it ring from the phone, and silence it once found.
  • rule: a « find me » from the phone beeps and buzzes the watch again and again, until a wheel press, which tells the phone.
    • how: once linked, the phone writes a recall of priority 8, waits 5 s, and the fake speaker must have rung at least three times; the story presses the wheel, and the phone must hear 11, and the speaker ring no more.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, press

PROMISE = "a « find me » from the phone beeps and buzzes the watch again and again, until a wheel press, which tells the phone"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)
RING_S = 5
QUIET_S = 5


def rings(speaker):
    return len([r for r in speaker.read_text().splitlines() if r == "ring"]) if speaker.exists() else 0


async def story(work):
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    heard = []
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=speaker, motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=wheel)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.hear_media(peer, heard.append)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "find me", priority=8, when=SENT)
            await asyncio.sleep(RING_S)
            press(wheel)
            for _ in range(100):
                if heard:
                    break
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            # a ring already started ends within its 500 ms
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
            rung = rings(speaker)
            await asyncio.sleep(QUIET_S)
            after = rings(speaker)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(speaker, "ring"))
    print(f"  rings: {rung} before the press, {after - rung} after; heard: {heard}")
    return rung >= 3 and after == rung and heard == [11]
what
my phone rings in my bag; the watch keeps buzzing until I answer or miss the call.
  • rule: a ringing call buzzes the watch again and again, until the phone says it stopped ringing.
    • how: once linked, the phone writes a recall of priority 6, waits 7 s, then writes one of priority 0; the fake motor must have buzzed at least three times before the 0, and never after it, and the fake speaker never rung.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = ("a ringing call buzzes the watch again and again, never rings it, until the phone says it"
           " stopped ringing")
CALL = "Phone: Alice: incoming call"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)
RING_S = 7
QUIET_S = 5


def buzzes(motor):
    return len([b for b in motor.read_text().splitlines() if b == "buzz"]) if motor.exists() else 0


async def story(work):
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=speaker, motor=motor)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.send_recall(peer, CALL, priority=6, when=SENT)
            await asyncio.sleep(RING_S)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, "", priority=0, when=SENT)
            # a buzz already started ends within its 750 ms
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
            ringing = buzzes(motor)
            await asyncio.sleep(QUIET_S)
            after = buzzes(motor)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(motor, "buzz"))
    rung = speaker.exists()
    print(f"  buzzes: {ringing} while ringing, {after - ringing} after the stop; rung: {rung}")
    return ringing >= 3 and after == ringing and not rung
what
a call I do not want rings my phone; I refuse it from the watch.
  • rule: a wheel press while a call rings stops the buzzing and tells the phone to refuse the call.
    • how: once linked, the phone writes a recall of priority 6, waits 5 s, and the story presses the wheel; the phone must hear 12, and the fake motor buzz no more.
  • rule: the press answers with a double buzz and « refusing the call », then shows the phone’s answer.
    • why: « the preqs to hangoff must have more feedvack »
    • how: the story’s phone answers 12 with « call refused » at priority 2, as mojito does; the screen must show both lines, and the motor a double buzz.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, press

PROMISE = ("a wheel press while a call rings stops the buzzing, tells the phone to refuse the call,"
           " and answers with a double buzz and the phone's answer")
CALL = "Phone: Alice: incoming call"
ANSWER = "call refused"
SENT = (2026, 10, 22, 7, 40)
RING_S = 5
QUIET_S = 5


def buzzes(motor):
    return len([b for b in motor.read_text().splitlines() if b == "buzz"]) if motor.exists() else 0


async def story(work):
    speaker = work / "speaker.log"
    motor = work / "motor.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    heard = []
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen,
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=speaker, motor=motor,
                                  wheel=wheel)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.hear_media(peer, heard.append)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, CALL, priority=6, when=SENT)
            await asyncio.sleep(RING_S)
            press(wheel)
            for _ in range(100):
                if heard:
                    break
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, ANSWER, priority=2, when=SENT)
            # a buzz already started ends within its 750 ms
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
            rung = buzzes(motor)
            await asyncio.sleep(QUIET_S)
            after = buzzes(motor)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(motor, "double"))
    doubles = motor.read_text().splitlines().count("double")
    shown = screen.read_text()
    told = "refusing the call" in shown and ANSWER in shown
    print(f"  buzzes: {rung} before the press, {after - rung} after; heard: {heard}; "
          f"doubles: {doubles}; told: {told}")
    return rung >= 3 and after == rung and heard == [12] and doubles == 1 and told
what
music plays on my phone in my pocket; I pause it, skip or go back from the watch.
  • rule: while the phone plays, the watch shows its title; a tap on it opens a pad whose left, middle and right go back, play or pause, and skip; the wheel closes it.
    • how: once linked, the phone writes a recall of priority 7, « Song: Artist »; the screen’s media row must show it; after a wheel press, the story taps the row, and the pad must open; it taps high on the screen’s middle, left, then right, and the phone must hear 2, 1, then 3; a wheel press must close the pad.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, press, written

PROMISE = "while the phone plays, the watch shows its title; a tap on it opens a pad whose left, middle and right go back, play or pause, and skip; the wheel closes it"
TITLE = "Song: Artist"
ROW_Y = 216
PAD_Y = 60


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    heard = []
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=wheel)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.hear_media(peer, heard.append)
            await companion.send_recall(peer, TITLE, priority=7)
            await written(work / "screen.log.media", "media " + TITLE)
            press(wheel)
            tap(taps, 120, ROW_Y)
            await written(work / "screen.log.media", "pad media")
            for x in (120, 20, 220):
                tap(taps, x, PAD_Y)
            for _ in range(100):
                if len(heard) == 3:
                    break
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            press(wheel)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(work / "screen.log.media", "pad off"))
    print(f"  heard: {heard}")
    return heard == [2, 1, 3]
what
my phone is somewhere in the flat, silent; I make it ring from the watch, and silence it once found.
  • rule: holding the wheel, then a tap on the pad’s right, rings the phone, and the next tap stops it.
    • how: once linked, the story holds the wheel and taps the actions pad’s right, and the phone must hear 9; then it taps once, and the phone must hear 10, and nothing more.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch, tap, hold, written

PROMISE = "holding the wheel, then a tap on the pad's right, rings the phone, and the next tap stops it"


async def heard_at_least(heard, count):
    for _ in range(100):
        if len(heard) >= count:
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)


async def story(work):
    screen = work / "screen.log"
    taps = work / "taps.log"
    wheel = work / "wheel.log"
    heard = []
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=screen, taps=taps,
                                  speaker=work / "speaker.log", motor=work / "motor.log",
                                  wheel=wheel)
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}") as peer:
            await companion.hear_media(peer, heard.append)
            # the watch says the phone's own name, « <name> linked »
            for _ in range(100):
                if any(line.endswith(" linked") for line in screen.read_text().splitlines()):
                    break
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            hold(wheel)
            await written(work / "screen.log.media", "pad actions")
            tap(taps, 200, 100)
            await heard_at_least(heard, 1)
            tap(taps, 120, 100)
            await heard_at_least(heard, 2)
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(screen, "phone found"))
    print(f"  heard: {heard}")
    return heard == [9, 10]
what
away from my phone for hours, the watch should not spend itself calling it.
  • rule: unlinked, the watch calls the phone on one beat that four Android scans each hear within 30 s, and still links.
    • why: after a reset, the watch waited 9 min unlinked before oxenhead found it.
    • how: no phone links; the story listens to the watch’s calls for 48 s: their gaps stay within a tenth of each other, and their beat, against each scan from any start, is heard within 30 s; then the phone links.
    • what: the four scans, listening a window in each interval: 0.5 s in 5 s, 0.512 s in 10.24 s, 0.14 s in 1.4 s, 0.183 s in 0.73 s.
    • what: bumble’s controller reads the interval’s 0.625 ms units as ms: 1.34 s comes 2.14 s apart.

import asyncio

import companion
from air import the_air, start_watch, stop_watch

PROMISE = "unlinked, the watch calls the phone on one beat that four Android scans each hear within 30 s, and still links"
LISTEN_S = 48
BUMBLE = 1.6
SCANS = ((500, 5000), (512, 10240), (140, 1400), (183, 730))
HEARD_WITHIN_S = 30


async def heard(transport):
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    heard = []
    async with await companion.open_transport(transport) as hci:
        device = companion.Device.with_hci("phone", companion.Address("F0:F1:F2:F3:F4:F5"),
                                           hci.source, hci.sink)
        await device.power_on()

        def on_advertisement(advertisement):
            name = advertisement.data.get(companion.AdvertisingData.Type.COMPLETE_LOCAL_NAME)
            if name == companion.NAME:
                heard.append(loop.time())

        device.on("advertisement", on_advertisement)
        await device.start_scanning(filter_duplicates=False)
        await asyncio.sleep(LISTEN_S)
        await device.stop_scanning()
    return [later - earlier for earlier, later in zip(heard, heard[1:])]


def longest_wait(beat_ms, window_ms, interval_ms, horizon_ms=600_000):
    longest = 0
    for start in range(0, interval_ms, 7):
        call = start
        while call < horizon_ms and call % interval_ms >= window_ms:
            call += beat_ms
        longest = max(longest, call - start)
    return longest / 1000


async def story(work):
    async with the_air(work) as (watch_pty, phone_pty):
        watch = await start_watch(watch_pty, mic=work / "none.wav", screen=work / "screen.log",
                                  taps=work / "taps.log", speaker=work / "speaker.log",
                                  motor=work / "motor.log")
        gaps = await heard(f"serial:{phone_pty}")
        async with companion.linked(f"serial:{phone_pty}"):
            pass
        await stop_watch(watch, once=(work / "screen.log", "waiting for the phone"))
    print(f"  gaps: {' / '.join(str(round(gap, 1)) for gap in gaps)}")
    if len(gaps) < 3:
        return False
    beat = round(sum(gaps) / len(gaps) / BUMBLE, 2)
    waits = [longest_wait(round(beat * 1000), window, interval) for window, interval in SCANS]
    print(f"  beat: {beat} s, longest waits: {' / '.join(map(str, waits))}")
    return max(gaps) < 1.1 * min(gaps) and max(waits) <= HEARD_WITHIN_S
what
from the desktop, I reach the watch through the phone’s relay, and leave it running after.
  • rule: a desktop that leaves the relay with bytes still waiting leaves none for the watch’s next link.
    • what: bytes left waiting reach the watch’s REPL as keys at its next link; a Ctrl-C among them stops its main.py, leaving it dead to taps and phone.
    • how: the story runs the phone’s companion with its android parts faked; a desktop sends a line while the watch is away and leaves; then the watch links and must be written nothing on REPL_IN.

import asyncio
import socket
import sys
import threading
import types
from unittest import mock

PROMISE = "a desktop that leaves the relay with bytes still waiting leaves none for the watch's next link"


class Dispatcher:
    gatt = None

    def __init__(self):
        self.written = []

    def write_characteristic(self, characteristic, data):
        self.written.append((characteristic, bytes(data)))

    def close_gatt(self):
        pass

    def _set_queue(self):
        pass


def android_fakes():
    able = types.ModuleType("able")
    able.GATT_SUCCESS = 0
    able.BluetoothDispatcher = Dispatcher
    filters = types.ModuleType("able.filters")
    filters.DeviceNameFilter = lambda name: name
    broadcast = types.ModuleType("android.broadcast")
    broadcast.BroadcastReceiver = mock.MagicMock()
    osc = types.ModuleType("helpers.osc")
    osc.oschandler = lambda *args, **kwargs: lambda handler: handler
    osc.to_app = lambda *args: None
    jnius = types.ModuleType("jnius")
    jnius.autoclass = mock.MagicMock()
    return {"able": able, "able.filters": filters, "android": types.ModuleType("android"),
            "android.broadcast": broadcast, "helpers": types.ModuleType("helpers"), "helpers.osc": osc,
            "jnius": jnius}


def free_port():
    with socket.socket() as probe:
        probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return probe.getsockname()[1]


async def said(lines, words):
    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
        while not any(words in line for line in lines):
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)


async def desktop(port, data):
    async with asyncio.timeout(10):
        while True:
            try:
                _, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
                break
            except OSError:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    writer.write(data)
    await writer.drain()
    writer.close()
    await writer.wait_closed()


async def story(work):
    with mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, android_fakes()):
        import twatch
    twatch.RELAY_PORT = free_port()
    twatch.show_playing = lambda: None
    twatch.link_state = lambda state: None
    lines = []
    companion = twatch.Companion(lines.append)
    threading.Thread(target=companion.serve_relay, daemon=True).start()
    await desktop(twatch.RELAY_PORT, b"print('left behind')\r\n")
    await said(lines, "relay closed")
    companion.steps.clear()
    companion.services = mock.MagicMock()
    companion.services.search.side_effect = lambda uuid: mock.MagicMock(name=uuid)
    companion.next_step()
    sent = [data for target, data in companion.written if target is companion.repl_in]
    print(f"  said: {' / '.join(lines)}")
    print(f"  sent at the link: {sent}")
    return not sent

           stay, reach, lightlog, heard, charge, chargelog, lost, turn, first, busy, relay, asleep, firmware,
           restore]
STORY_LIMIT_S = 120


async def main(names):
    reds = 0
    for story in [story for story in STORIES if story.__name__ in names] or STORIES:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as work:
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(STORY_LIMIT_S):

            except Exception as error:

        print(f"{'green' if green else 'red  '} :: {story.PROMISE}")

    return reds


sys.exit(asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1:])))
how
the air is two bumble controllers linked together, one pty for the watch, one for the phone. 
import asyncio
import contextlib
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


async def appears(path):
    for _ in range(100):
        if path.exists():
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    raise TimeoutError(path)


@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def the_air(work):
    watch_pty, phone_pty = work / "watch.pty", work / "phone.pty"
    controllers = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        sys.executable, "-I", "-m", "bumble.apps.controllers",
        f"pty:{watch_pty}", f"pty:{phone_pty}",
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        await appears(watch_pty)
        await appears(phone_pty)
        yield watch_pty, phone_pty
    finally:
        controllers.terminate()
        await controllers.wait()
how
the watch is its own micropython process, finding the fakes where the watch has hardware, its microphone hearing the file the story names, its touch reading taps from the file it names, its screen, speaker and motor writing to the files it names, its battery at the percent it names, charging while the file it names exists, its wifi joining unless it names no network, its errors kept beside its screen’s file unless it names another, and its chosen phone beside it too.
  • why: it runs from the fakes’ directory, lest a stray main.py where the harness started be the one it runs.
async def start_watch(watch_pty, mic, screen, taps, speaker, motor, battery=80, dark=False, wheel=None,
                      charger=None, network=True, errors=None):
    return await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        os.environ["TWATCH_MICROPYTHON"], str(ROOT / "watch" / "main.py"), cwd=ROOT / "fake",
        env={**os.environ, "MICROPYPATH": str(ROOT / "fake"), "MICROPYBTUART": str(watch_pty),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_MIC": str(mic), "TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN": str(screen),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_TAPS": str(taps), "TWATCH_FAKE_BATTERY": str(battery),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_SPEAKER": str(speaker), "TWATCH_FAKE_MOTOR": str(motor),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_DARK": "1" if dark else "",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_WHEEL": str(wheel) if wheel else "",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_CHARGER": str(charger) if charger else "",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_NO_NETWORK": "" if network else "1",
             "TWATCH_FAKE_ERRORS": str(errors or Path(screen).with_name("errors.log")),
             "TWATCH_FAKE_PHONE": str(Path(screen).with_name("phone.txt"))})

the story waits, up to 10 s unless it names longer, for a fake to write a line. 
async def written(path, line, seconds=10):
    for _ in range(seconds * 20):
        if path.exists() and line in path.read_text().splitlines():
            return
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    raise TimeoutError(f"{path.name} never said {line}")
