async def stop_watch(watch, once):
    try:
        await written(*once)
    finally:
        watch.terminate()
        await watch.wait()
how
what the fake microphone hears is half a second of a 440 Hz tone, 8 kHz, 16 bits, mono. 
import math
import struct
import wave


def spoken_thought(path):
    rate = 8000
    frames = b"".join(
        struct.pack("<h", int(12000 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 440 * n / rate)))
        for n in range(rate // 2))
    with wave.open(str(path), "wb") as wav:
        wav.setnchannels(1)
        wav.setsampwidth(2)
        wav.setframerate(rate)
        wav.writeframes(frames)

the watch’s firmware

what
the watch runs micropython 1.27 for the esp32-s3 with octal psram, carrying the pdm pull request.
  • how: its two code commits are fetched by hash, the second’s ESP_ERROR_CHECK written check_esp_err, as micropython 1.27 names it.
  • how: between two looks, the chip light-sleeps on its own, meant to keep its ble link; not yet tried.
    • how: freertos idles tickless, and machine.freq, which boot.py calls, lets the chip sleep.
    • how: the ble controller sleeps between its connection events, clocked by the main crystal.
    • why: the watch has no 32 kHz crystal wired to the chip; the main one stays powered in sleep, a few mA, against tens awake.
    • scope: on usb, the serial port keeps it awake, so the repl stays usable there.
    • how: micropython’s sleep_ms waits its span one 10 ms tick at a time, while the chip sleeps only when no task runs for 3 ticks8; so its wait asks for all the whole ticks left but one at once.
      • why: « It was inc’edible hpw the pçnetime could be used one week wçthoit charge. by contrast, the micropython os was only one day »
  • how: the flash holds two firmware slots, each as large as micropython’s single one9, the files after them, meant to let a new firmware go over the phone into the idle slot; that transfer is not yet written.
    • why: « i’m far from the desktop. can we flasn anyway? »
  • how: esp-idf counts the time spent in each power mode and the light sleeps made and refused, and esp32.pm_dump() hands python that count as text, with the power locks held.
    • why: « so 4 is a measure, and 2 is an improvement ? Why make a false choice then, it’s obviously 4 AND 2 »
    • how: each change to micropython’s C is a diff here, applied to the pinned source; a diff that no longer applies stops the build.
      • why: « how will we ensure reproducibility and maintaonability ? »

--- a/ports/esp32/modesp32.c
+++ b/ports/esp32/modesp32.c
@@ -27,2 +27,3 @@
 #include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
 #include <string.h>
@@ -32,2 +33,3 @@
 #include "driver/gpio.h"
+#include "esp_pm.h"
 #include "esp_heap_caps.h"
@@ -315,4 +317,16 @@
 static MP_DEFINE_CONST_FUN_OBJ_0(esp32_idf_task_info_obj, esp32_idf_task_info);
 #endif
+
+static mp_obj_t esp32_pm_dump(void) {
+    char *text = NULL;
+    size_t size = 0;
+    FILE *stream = open_memstream(&text, &size);
+    esp_pm_dump_locks(stream);
+    fclose(stream);
+    mp_obj_t dump = mp_obj_new_str(text, size);
+    free(text);
+    return dump;
+}
+static MP_DEFINE_CONST_FUN_OBJ_0(esp32_pm_dump_obj, esp32_pm_dump);

 static const mp_rom_map_elem_t esp32_module_globals_table[] = {
@@ -341,4 +355,5 @@
     #endif
     { MP_ROM_QSTR(MP_QSTR_idf_heap_info), MP_ROM_PTR(&esp32_idf_heap_info_obj) },
+    { MP_ROM_QSTR(MP_QSTR_pm_dump), MP_ROM_PTR(&esp32_pm_dump_obj) },
     #if CONFIG_FREERTOS_USE_TRACE_FACILITY
     { MP_ROM_QSTR(MP_QSTR_idf_task_info), MP_ROM_PTR(&esp32_idf_task_info_obj) },


let
  pins = import ./pins.nix;
  inherit (pins.nixpkgs) fetchpatch;
  pdm-patches = [
    (fetchpatch {
      url = "https://github.com/micropython/micropython/commit/ec24a150e02b7eff1271b59f0667cdb94a7aef62.patch";
      hash = "sha256-Hu+0eT915QhupvO5s6+HYLsEzcPFTMFIjDowxnQLZDQ=";
    })
    (fetchpatch {
      url = "https://github.com/micropython/micropython/commit/843085b7cf25d93aa712cf807298ae293ac64a8b.patch";
      postFetch = "sed -i 's/ESP_ERROR_CHECK(/check_esp_err(/' $out";
      hash = "sha256-3Je5VFn3P8rVa/oNOCxKluevPgErqk53MYDXNDk/1ZM=";
    })
  ];
in
pins.esp-pkgs.mkShell {
  buildInputs = [ pins.esp-pkgs.esp-idf-esp32s3 ];
  MICROPYTHON_PDM_SRC = pins.nixpkgs.applyPatches {
    name = "micropython-pdm-src";
    src = pins.nixpkgs.micropython.src;
    patches = pdm-patches ++ [ ./patches/pm-dump.patch ];
    patchFlags = [ "-p1" "--fuzz=0" ];
    postPatch = ''
      cat >> ports/esp32/boards/ESP32_GENERIC_S3/sdkconfig.board <<EOF
      CONFIG_FREERTOS_USE_TICKLESS_IDLE=y
      CONFIG_BT_CTRL_MODEM_SLEEP=y
      CONFIG_BT_CTRL_MODEM_SLEEP_MODE_1=y
      CONFIG_BT_CTRL_LPCLK_SEL_MAIN_XTAL=y
      CONFIG_BT_CTRL_MAIN_XTAL_PU_DURING_LIGHT_SLEEP=y
      CONFIG_USJ_NO_AUTO_LS_ON_CONNECTION=y
      CONFIG_PM_PROFILING=y
      CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM_FILENAME="partitions-twatch-ota.csv"
      EOF
      cat > ports/esp32/partitions-twatch-ota.csv <<EOF
      nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,   0x4000,
      otadata,  data, ota,     0xd000,   0x2000,
      phy_init, data, phy,     0xf000,   0x1000,
      ota_0,    app,  ota_0,   0x10000,  0x1F0000,
      ota_1,    app,  ota_1,   0x200000, 0x1F0000,
      EOF
      substituteInPlace ports/esp32/modmachine.c \
        --replace-fail ".light_sleep_enable = false" ".light_sleep_enable = true"
      substituteInPlace ports/esp32/mphalport.c \
        --replace-fail "ulTaskNotifyTake(pdFALSE, 1);" \
          "ulTaskNotifyTake(pdFALSE, (us - dt) / 1000 / portTICK_PERIOD_MS - 1);"
    '';
  };
}
how
one script builds it from scratch, into build/firmware.bin. 
#!/usr/bin/env nix-shell
#!nix-shell -i bash firmware-shell.nix
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
work=$here/build/micropython
rm -rf "$work"
mkdir -p "$here/build"
cp -r "$MICROPYTHON_PDM_SRC" "$work"
chmod -R u+w "$work"
make -C "$work/mpy-cross"
make -C "$work/ports/esp32" BOARD=ESP32_GENERIC_S3 BOARD_VARIANT=SPIRAM_OCT
cp "$work/ports/esp32/build-ESP32_GENERIC_S3-SPIRAM_OCT/firmware.bin" "$here/build/firmware.bin"
  • scope: esp-idf 5.5.2 rewrites micropython’s lockfile, written for 5.5.1; its two components, mdns 1.1.0 and tinyusb e4c0ec3c, stay those it pins.

the watch is reached over its usb serial port, with esptool and mpremote from the pinned nixpkgs, and over the air with bleak.
  • why: the python with bleak comes first, since the pythons esptool and mpremote carry would shadow it.

how
flashing erases the watch whole, then writes the firmware at the start of the flash.
  • how: the watch enters flashing mode by hand, as the real trial draws; BOOT and RST are both reachable with the back closed.
  • why: behind this desktop’s usb hubs, esptool cannot pull the reset line, so the watch enters flashing mode by hand; once flashed, a press on RST starts the new firmware.

#!/usr/bin/env nix-shell
#!nix-shell -i bash device-shell.nix
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
port=${1:-/dev/ttyACM0}
rm -rf "$here/sent"
esptool --chip esp32s3 --port "$port" --before no-reset --after no-reset \
        write-flash --erase-all 0 "$here/build/firmware.bin"

the erase takes every file with it, so after the press on RST restore-watch.sh puts them back, main.py with them, and restarts the watch.

how
once the watch holds two slots, a new firmware comes over its wifi REPL: over-wifi.sh update-firmware.sh; the image is copied to the watch, written into the idle slot, checked against its hash, and only then made the boot slot and started.
  • why: « again? ypu were supposed rtouse two slot to allow flashing OTA »
  • why: over mojito’s bluetooth relay, 1.7 MB would take hours: 4.9 KB took 79 s.
  • what: a firmware that boots but misbehaves stays: no rollback is built in; the old slot is untouched until the next update.
  • how: the app image is the firmware from 0x10000 on, its trailing erased bytes dropped.
import sys

APP_AT = 0x10000

firmware = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()[APP_AT:]
open(sys.argv[2], "wb").write(firmware.rstrip(b"\xff"))
  • how: the update’s log alone tells where it is: each step with its time, the copy in twentieths, « installing », the watch’s « ota: » line, then « done » or « failed ».
    • how: the image goes in twenty pieces, each appended on the watch as it lands.
    • how: as each piece lands, the watch shows and prints its percent and the time left, the time so far spread over the pieces still to come.

import time

import screen

_total = 0
_done = 0
_start = 0


def start(total):
    global _total, _done, _start
    _total, _done, _start = total, 0, time.ticks_ms()
    open("app.bin", "wb").close()


def _left(ms):
    s = ms // 1000
    if s >= 3600:
        return "%d h %02d" % (s // 3600, s % 3600 // 60)
    if s >= 60:
        return "%d min" % (s // 60)
    return "%d s" % s


def add():
    global _done
    block = bytearray(4096)
    with open("app.bin", "ab") as whole, open("app.part", "rb") as part:
        while True:
            got = part.readinto(block)
            if not got:
                break
            whole.write(memoryview(block)[:got])
    _done += 1
    line = "firmware %d %%" % (100 * _done // _total)
    if _done < _total:
        spent = time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _start)
        line += ", %s left" % _left(spent * (_total - _done) // _done)
    print(line)
    screen.say(line)
how
« done » comes only from the watch’s « written and checked », not from mpremote’s exit.

#!/usr/bin/env nix-shell
#!nix-shell -i bash device-shell.nix
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
port=$1
image=$here/build/app.bin
pieces=$here/build/app.pieces
PIECES=20
step() { echo "$(date +%T) $*"; }
step "cutting the image"
python3 -I "$here/app-image.py" "$here/build/firmware.bin" "$image"
digest=$(sha256sum "$image")
rm -rf "$pieces"
mkdir -p "$pieces"
split -n "$PIECES" -d -a 3 "$image" "$pieces/"
step "copying $(stat -c %s "$image") bytes in $PIECES pieces"
copies=(cp "$here/watch/pieces.py" :pieces.py + exec "import pieces; pieces.start($PIECES)")
for piece in "$pieces"/*; do
    copies+=(+ cp "$piece" :app.part + exec "pieces.add()")
done
copies+=(+ exec "import os; os.remove('app.part'); print('installing'); import ota; ota.install('app.bin', '${digest%% *}')")
PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 mpremote connect "$port" resume "${copies[@]}" | tee "$here/build/ota.out"
if grep -q "ota: written and checked" "$here/build/ota.out"; then
    step "done"
else
    step "failed"
    exit 1
fi
how
on the watch, the image is written block by block, read back for its hash, and the watch restarts on it only if the hash matches.
import binascii
import hashlib
import os

import esp32
import machine

BLOCK = 4096


def install(path, digest):
    target = esp32.Partition(esp32.Partition.RUNNING).get_next_update()
    size = os.stat(path)[6]
    blocks = (size + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
    block = bytearray(BLOCK)
    with open(path, "rb") as image:
        for at in range(blocks):
            got = image.readinto(block)
            for i in range(got, BLOCK):
                block[i] = 0xFF
            target.writeblocks(at, block)
    check = hashlib.sha256()
    for at in range(blocks):
        target.readblocks(at, block)
        check.update(block[:min(BLOCK, size - at * BLOCK)])
    if binascii.hexlify(check.digest()).decode() != digest:
        print("ota: hash mismatch, not booted")
        return
    os.remove(path)
    target.set_boot()
    print("ota: written and checked, restarting")
    machine.reset()
how
the watch’s modules go onto its flash; which main.py it boots, the trial or the mic test, is put by the script that plays it.
  • how: the watch first says « updating », and keeps it until the reset that ends the update; a freshly flashed watch, with no screen module yet, says nothing.
    • why: over oxenhead the copy takes minutes; the screen would otherwise stay frozen on its last line.
  • how: under « updating », a line shows the file being sent and a bar of all that is sent so far, redrawn as each 512-byte piece lands.
    • why: mpremote’s cp says nothing to the watch until a file is whole; one file looked hung for 79 s.
    • how: the desk sends each piece itself, in base64, into <name>.part, renamed once whole, so a cut update never leaves a half module to import.
  • how: only the files changed since they were last sent go, all in one connection; the desk keeps each sent file’s hash in sent/, which a flash empties.
    • why: asked which files differ, the watch hashes each one and answers over ble, a round trip a file, where an update most often changes one.
  • how: then, shipped or not, the watch hashes every file of the list in one round trip, and a line « name desk’s sha256 watch’s sha256 » is printed for each; a mismatch, or a file missing, fails the run and forgets that file’s hash in sent/, so the next run sends it again.
    • why: « can ypu make the hpdate script outpjt the sha of the delloyed files to make confirmation trivial ? »
    • what: untested: no story runs the deploy; its first run on the watch is its test.

#!/usr/bin/env nix-shell
#!nix-shell -i bash device-shell.nix
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
port=${1:-/dev/ttyACM0}
sent="$here/sent"
mkdir -p "$sent"
PIECE=512
files=("$here/watch/link.py" "$here/watch/repl.py" "$here/watch/ota.py"
       "$here/device/mic.py" "$here/device/screen.py"
       "$here/device/speaker.py" "$here/device/motor.py" "$here/device/touch.py"
       "$here/device/wifi.py" "$here/device/battery.py" "$here/device/wheel.py" "$here/device/sleep.py"
       "$here/device/boot.py" "$here/device/clock.py" "$here/device/glyphs.py" "$here/device/flash.py"
       "$ST7789PY/lib/st7789py.py" "$ST7789PY/romfonts/vga2_8x16.py")
[ -e "$here/device/wifi_secret.py" ] && files+=("$here/device/wifi_secret.py")


check() {
    local names="" status=0 file name mine theirs hashes
    for file in "${files[@]}"; do
        names+="'$(basename "$file")',"
    done
    hashes=$(mpremote connect "$port" resume exec "$(cat <<EOF
import binascii, hashlib
for name in ($names):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    try:
        with open(name, 'rb') as f:
            while True:
                piece = f.read($PIECE)
                if not piece:
                    break
                digest.update(piece)
        print(name, binascii.hexlify(digest.digest()).decode())
    except OSError:
        print(name, 'missing')
EOF
)" | tr -d '\r')
    for file in "${files[@]}"; do
        name=$(basename "$file")
        mine=$(sha256sum < "$file" | cut -d' ' -f1)
        theirs=$(printf '%s\n' "$hashes" | awk -v name="$name" '$1 == name {print $2}')
        echo "$name $mine $theirs"
        if [ "$mine" != "$theirs" ]; then
            rm -f "$sent/$name"
            status=1
        fi
    done
    return $status
}


changed=()
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
    sha256sum < "$file" | cmp -s - "$sent/$(basename "$file")" || changed+=("$file")
done
if [ ${#changed[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    check
    exit
fi
total=0
for file in "${changed[@]}"; do
    total=$((total + $(stat -c %s "$file")))
done
copies=()
done_bytes=0
for file in "${changed[@]}"; do
    name=$(basename "$file")
    size=$(stat -c %s "$file")
    copies+=(+ exec "open('$name.part','wb').close()")
    for ((offset = 0; offset < size; offset += PIECE)); do
        piece=$(tail -c +$((offset + 1)) "$file" | head -c "$PIECE" | base64 -w0)
        done_bytes=$((done_bytes + (size - offset < PIECE ? size - offset : PIECE)))
        copies+=(+ exec "f=open('$name.part','ab');f.write(a2b_base64('$piece'));f.close();show('$name',$done_bytes,$total)")
    done
    copies+=(+ exec "os.rename('$name.part','$name')")
done
mpremote connect "$port" resume \
         exec "$(cat <<'EOF'
import os
from binascii import a2b_base64
try:
    import screen
    screen.say("updating")
    screen.say("")
    def show(name, sent, total):
        filled = 12 * sent // total
        screen.redo("{} {}{} {}%".format(name[:10], "#" * filled, "." * (12 - filled), 100 * sent // total))
except ImportError:
    def show(name, sent, total):
        pass
EOF
)" \
         "${copies[@]}"
for file in "${changed[@]}"; do
    sha256sum < "$file" > "$sent/$(basename "$file")"
done

how
at boot, the pmu’s dc4 and dc5, « No use » in LilyGo’s library, and bldo1, its gps power, go off: bits 3 and 4 of 0x80, bit 4 of 0x90.
  • why: they were found on, fed for nothing; the gnss track will turn bldo1 back on.
import machine
from machine import I2C, Pin

PMU = 0x34
DCDC_ONOFF, LDO_ONOFF = 0x80, 0x90
DC4_DC5, BLDO1 = 0b11000, 0b10000

machine.freq(80_000_000)
_i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(10), scl=Pin(11), freq=400_000)
for register, bits in ((DCDC_ONOFF, DC4_DC5), (LDO_ONOFF, BLDO1)):
    _i2c.writeto_mem(PMU, register, bytes((_i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, register, 1)[0] & ~bits,)))
how
once switched on, the watch joins the wifi as « twatch » and serves its REPL on tcp port 23, so it is reached without usb.
  • rule: the watch starts with the wifi off; the bar’s button switches it on, and it goes off again after 30 min with nothing typed in its REPL.
  • rule: the phone never waits on the wifi: the watch calls out to it first, and gives up on a wifi not joined within 30 s.
  • how: the wifi’s name and password live in wifi_secret.py, never in this note: the tangle asks clk for the password and writes it in device/, and the deploy copies it to the watch.
  • how: the REPL is hooked as webrepl does it, the socket’s callback waking os.dupterm, so a ctrl-C over the wifi stops a running main.py.
  • how: switching on only starts joining; the REPL’s port opens at the first look that finds the wifi joined.
import network
import os
import socket
import time

import wifi_secret

PORT = 23
_CALLBACK = 20
_station = network.WLAN(network.STA_IF)
_server = None
_used = time.ticks_ms()


def _typed(client):
    global _used
    _used = time.ticks_ms()
    os.dupterm_notify(client)


def _accept(server):
    client, _ = server.accept()
    client.setblocking(False)
    client.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, _CALLBACK, _typed)
    os.dupterm(client)


def idle_ms():
    return time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _used)


def on():
    global _used
    _used = time.ticks_ms()
    network.hostname("twatch")
    _station.active(True)
    _station.connect(wifi_secret.SSID, wifi_secret.PASSWORD)


def joined():
    global _server
    if not _station.isconnected():
        return None
    if _server is not None:
        return _station.ifconfig()[0]
    _server = socket.socket()
    _server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    _server.bind(("0.0.0.0", PORT))
    _server.listen(1)
    _server.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, _CALLBACK, _accept)
    return _station.ifconfig()[0]


def off():
    global _server
    os.dupterm(None)
    if _server is not None:
        _server.close()
        _server = None
    _station.active(False)

the watch keeps the time the phone gives in its rtc; until it is given, it knows none.
  • how: an rtc never set starts in 2000, so a later year is a time given.
import machine
import time


def set(when):
    year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second = when
    machine.RTC().datetime((year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second, 0))


def now():
    when = time.localtime()
    return when if when[0] > 2000 else None
how
under test, the clock is a fake that runs from the time given, on the desktop’s seconds. 
import time

_offset = None


def set(when):
    global _offset
    year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second = when
    _offset = time.mktime((year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday, 0)) - time.time()


def now():
    return None if _offset is None else time.localtime(time.time() + _offset)

how
here, socat turns that port into a pty, and any script taking the watch’s port runs through it.
  • how: the watch is reached by the name « twatch », the router’s to resolve; TWATCH_HOST names it otherwise, as TWATCH_HOST=192.168.1.23 over-wifi.sh play-oxenhead.sh.
  • how: from afar, the same reaches the watch through oxenhead, which relays its port 9721 to the watch’s REPL over ble: TWATCH_HOST=oxenhead TWATCH_PORT=9721 over-wifi.sh deploy-watch.sh.
  • how: mpremote then =resume=s, since a soft reset would close the socket it talks through.
  • how: a reset over the wifi cuts the link it travels on, so its mpremote fails, and that is ignored.
  • rule: each bridge links its own tty, so two at once never take each other’s.
  • how: a watch that has not answered within REACH_S seconds is out of reach, said in one line, naming the bar’s « W » to tap, before anything is sent.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
host=${TWATCH_HOST:-twatch}
port=${TWATCH_PORT:-23}
REACH_S=5
if ! timeout "$REACH_S" bash -c ": < /dev/tcp/$host/$port" 2> /dev/null; then
    echo "cannot reach $host:$port: tap the watch's bar so « W » joins, or start its relay" >&2
    exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$here/build"
tty=$(mktemp -u "$here/build/watch-XXXXXX.tty")
nix-shell "$here/device-shell.nix" \
          --run "exec socat pty,link=$tty,raw,echo=0 tcp:$host:$port" &
bridge=$!
trap 'kill $bridge' EXIT
while [ ! -e "$tty" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
"$@" "$tty"
how
out, only mojito is with me; while it holds the watch, its poc app relays the same port 9721, reached at its vpn address: over-mojito.sh deploy-watch.sh.
  • why: no adb out of home, and the vpn reaches mojito where ssh does, with no tunnel to keep.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
TWATCH_HOST=192.168.2.34 TWATCH_PORT=9721 exec "$here/over-wifi.sh" "$@"
how
a battery mark, taken whenever I like through mojito: battery-mark.sh reads the watch’s charge and voltage, keeps them with the time in battery-marks.txt, and tells the drain since the previous mark.
  • what: the read restarts main.py on the watch.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
here=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")
if [ "${1:-}" = --read ]; then
    nix-shell "$here/device-shell.nix" --run "mpremote connect $2 resume exec 'import battery; print(*battery.level())'"
    nix-shell "$here/device-shell.nix" --run "mpremote connect $2 resume reset" > /dev/null || true
    exit 0
fi
marks=$here/battery-marks.txt
level=$("$here/over-mojito.sh" "$0" --read | tail -n 1)
read -r percent millivolts <<< "$level"
now=$(date +%s)
previous=$(tail -n 1 "$marks" 2> /dev/null || true)
echo "$now $(date -d "@$now" '+%F %T') $percent $millivolts" >> "$marks"
echo "$(date -d "@$now" '+%F %T'): $percent %, $millivolts mV"
if [ -n "$previous" ]; then
    awk -v now="$now" -v percent="$percent" -v millivolts="$millivolts" '{
        hours = (now - $1) / 3600
        printf "since %s %s, %.1f h: %.1f mV/h, %.1f %%/h\n", $2, $3, hours, ($5 - millivolts) / hours, ($4 - percent) / hours
    }' <<< "$previous"
fi
how
mojito’s app is restarted by stopping and starting it, as root over ssh, nothing more; the script waits for the companion to say « ready », then sends the app to the background.
  • why: a twatch.py tangled to mojito runs only once the app starts again.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
ssh mojito su -c "'logcat -c; am force-stop eu.konubinix.konixpoc; am start -n eu.konubinix.konixpoc/org.kivy.android.PythonActivity'"
for _ in $(seq 60); do
    if ssh mojito su -c "'logcat -d'" | grep -q "twatch: ready"; then
        ssh mojito curl -sS -m 10 -w '%{http_code}\\n' http://127.0.0.1:9717/background
        exit 0
    fi
    timeout 2 tail -f /dev/null
done
echo "mojito's companion never said ready"
exit 1
how
what mojito’s companion last said of its link, as root over ssh: mojito-link-log.sh 15. 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
lines=${1:-15}
ssh mojito "date; su -c \"logcat -d | grep -E 'app.twatch|Traceback' | grep -v 'recall ' | tail -n $lines\"" | cut -c1-200
how
the same for oxenhead, over adb: oxenhead-link-log.sh 15. 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
lines=${1:-15}
date
adb -s oxenhead:5555 logcat -d -s konixpoc:* | grep -E 'app.twatch|Traceback' | grep -v 'recall ' | tail -n "$lines" | cut -c1-200
how
waiting for the watch to link to oxenhead, after a reset or a deploy, ends as soon as it says « ready », or after as many seconds as given: oxenhead-wait-ready.sh 120.
  • why: « create a better command than “timeout 90 adb -s oxenhead:5555 logcat -T 1 -s konixpoc:* …” », which always waited its 90 s, though the watch linked in 70.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
seconds=${1:-120}
since=$(adb -s oxenhead:5555 shell date "'+%m-%d %H:%M:%S.000'")
timeout "$seconds" adb -s oxenhead:5555 logcat -T "$since" -s konixpoc:* \
    | awk '/app.twatch/ { print substr($0, 1, 200); fflush() } /twatch: ready/ { found = 1; exit } END { exit !found }'
status=$?
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "the watch did not say ready within $seconds s"
fi
exit "$status"

the voice, on the watch

what
the watch waits for the phone, then, while it is linked, shows each recall the phone sends, and records from a tap on the screen to the next, 2 min at most, then sends over ble, writing each step on it; when the phone leaves, it waits for it again.
how
a recall’s priority is ntfy’s, 1 to 5: 1 is written on a dark screen without lighting it, 2 lights it, 3 also buzzes once, 4 buzzes and rings, 5 buzzes and rings three times.
  • how: 6 is a ringing call: it buzzes, never rings, then buzzes every 2 s until a recall of priority 0 says the call stopped ringing, the wheel is pressed, or 60 s have passed.
    • why: « the watch must vibrate when calling, but not ring »
  • how: 8 is the phone looking for the watch: as 6, but each buzz every 2 s also rings, and the wheel press that stops it sends 11 on the media characteristic, so the phone knows.
  • how: 7 is what the phone plays: its text goes to the media row, not to the lines, empty when nothing plays; a tap on that row opens the pad, the whole screen in three tall columns, where a tap on the left, middle or right one goes back, plays or pauses, or skips.
    • why: « it’s not practical to have to be precise and target the bar »
    • how: the wheel closes the pad, back to the lines, as do the 5 s dark and a new line that lights.
  • how: 1 and 2 are for senders too noisy to be heard each time.
  • how: a recall that says again what the last one said, in the same minute, is left out.
    • why: some ntfy publishers post each message twice, once with the hour before it.
how
while a recording goes out, its line counts « sending 45 % », redone in place each 5 %, then becomes « sent in 12 s »; the garbage it left is then collected.
  • how: as a send starts, the screen turns read-only, and stays so; the wheel makes it touchable again.
    • why: a tap, or a stray pulse of the panel, during the send would start another recording.
how
a send that fails says « send stalled, kept », and the recording waits for the next link.
how
a recall’s line starts with when the phone took it, « 08:42 », or « 22/10 08:42 » when not today.
how
unlinked, a recording is kept and sent at the next link; while one is kept, a tap records nothing more.
  • why: more would fill the ram.
how
the screen’s bottom row is a button that switches the wifi on and off; it also shows the battery’s percent, blue while charging, its voltage, the wifi, the phone link and the ram free, « 95% 4.06V W B 3.2M ».
  • how: the wifi is one « W », on black: grey off, yellow joining, green joined, red not found.
    • why: « save space -> wifi on an wifi off becomes a colored “W” »

WIFI_TINTS = {"off": "grey", "joining": "yellow", "joined": "green", "not found": "red"}
how
the phone link is one « B » after it, on black: yellow while waiting for the phone, green linked.
  • why: « add “B”, like “W” »

PHONE_TINTS = {"waiting": "yellow", "linked": "green"}
how
a refresh reads again from the watch all the screen shows, the bar and the hour, and redraws them; the lines are not read again, each being said once.
  • why: « there lust be a concept of screen refresh »
  • how: it comes at start, each minute the screen is lit, when the wheel makes the screen touch-sensitive, and at each tap on a dark or read-only screen.
how
once joined, the wifi’s address is said as a line.
how
the watch starts lit read-only, lest a touch while it boots record.
how
every tap or press on a lit screen restarts its 5 s before dark.
  • why: « every interaction with the watch must reset the 5s timer »
how
a tap on a dark screen lights it before its tick and redraw, so it shows at once.
  • why: the tick and the redraw kept a dark tap from showing for 0.5 to 0.9 s.
how
a tap on a dark or read-only screen lights it read-only 5 s more, where taps record nothing; the wheel lights it touch-sensitive, dark or read-only, and darkens it when touch-sensitive.
how
holding the wheel, about 1.5 s, opens the actions pad, three tall columns, from any screen: « torch » on the left, the phone to link with in the middle, « find phone » on the right; holding it again, or a press, closes it.
  • how: a tap on its top row, the names, turns it to its second page, « stay lit », and back.
    • why: « the action pad could have several screens », « swipe and tap may conflict »
how
a tap on the middle column steps through « any phone » and each phone’s name seen linking since start, kept in phone.txt across restarts; the pad stays open.
  • how: a phone other than the chosen one is dropped as soon as it says its name, and said so, without lighting; choosing drops a linked phone that is not the one.
  • why: « can we in a menu of watch decide whar phàneto use ? »
  • what: the phone left out keeps looking for the watch, so its battery pays for it.
  • why: « even the torch is barely usable. the wheel is not responsive enough » for presses timed under 0.5 s.
  • how: the hold is the pmu’s own long-press signal, latched as the short press is.
  • how: the torch is put out by any tap or press, back to the read-only screen.
how
a picture the phone sends fills the screen as its half-rows come, the screen lit; any tap or press puts the lines back.
  • why: « a way to send a display a picture on watch ? »
  • how: « find phone » rings the phone, code 9 on MEDIA, saying « find phone sent »; the next tap or press, within the minute the phone rings, says it was found, code 10.
how
between looks, the watch naps 50 ms while lit and 1 s while dark.
  • why: dark is most of the day, and each look wakes the chip; the panel and the wheel latch a tap or a press until looked at, so none is lost.
  • how: the dark nap is cut in 100 ms slices and ends as soon as a finger lands on the panel; while one is on it, the watch naps as when lit, until it lifts.
    • why: « tap to wake is not react_ve enough »: a tap took up to 2 s, a look to see the finger, another to see it lift.
  • how: the lit nap is cut in 20 ms slices, too short for the chip to light-sleep.
    • how: each wake sets the backlight’s pwm up afresh, as a light sleep leaves it dead.
      • why: « screen stays dark. i feel vibrations »
    • why: « stroboscopically lit+dark+lit »: the backlight’s pwm stops while the chip light-sleeps.
how
touch-sensitive, a finger dragged down shows older lines, a row per 16 px, and dragged up newer ones; the wheel’s turn sends nothing, so it can’t.
how
under 15 %, every 5 min until it charges, the watch lights its screen with « battery low: 14 % », buzzes and rings; it looks each minute, lit or dark.
how
the top row shows the hour and the date, « 07:42 Thu 22/10 », from the time the phone gives at each link; it is redrawn whenever lit and the minute changes.
how
an error the main loop does not handle is shown, its traceback added to errors.log on the flash, the last 4 KB kept, and the watch restarts; at each link, the file goes to the phone on ERRORS, a line per notification, and is deleted once all went out.
  • why: « log excep(ions somewhere boot resistant and at next lçnk send to phone and purge »
how
at each link, then each hour while linked, the watch sends its charge as a line on CHARGE, « charge 80 % 3900 mV », « charging » added on the charger; the phone logs it as « watch charge: … ».
  • why: « 2 »: a charge sent on ERRORS read as an hourly watch error in the phone’s log.
  • what: the story sees the line at the link only; the hourly one stays untested, no story waits an hour.

import bluetooth
import gc
import io
import os
import sys
import time

import battery
import clock
import flash
import link
import mic
import motor
import screen
import sleep
import speaker
import touch
import wheel
import wifi

GAUGE_EVERY_MS = 60_000
CHARGE_EVERY_MS = 3_600_000
MARK_EVERY_MS = 3_600_000
ERRORS_KEPT = 4096
WIFI_JOIN_MS = 30_000
WIFI_IDLE_MS = 1_800_000
RECORD_MAX_S = 120
LOW_PERCENT = 15
SWIPE_PX = 16
ALARM_EVERY_MS = 300_000
LIT_NAP_MS = 50
AWAKE_SLICE_MS = 20
DARK_NAP_MS = 1000
DARK_SLICE_MS = 100
RING_EVERY_MS = 2_000
RING_FOR_MS = 60_000
# the media row's left, middle and right thirds: back, play or pause, skip
MEDIA_CODES = (1, 2, 3)
FIND_PHONE = 9
PHONE_FOUND = 10
WATCH_FOUND = 11
REFUSE_CALL = 12
CALL = 6
FIND_ME = 8
FIND_FOR_MS = 60_000
DAYS =("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
_wifi = "off"
_phone = "waiting"
_gauged = time.ticks_ms()
_checked = time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), -GAUGE_EVERY_MS)
_alarmed = None
_told = None
_marked = None
_woke = time.ticks_ms()
_awake = 0
_turns = 0
_slices = 0
_slept = sleep.counts()


def busy_note():
    global _awake, _turns, _slices, _woke, _slept
    now = time.ticks_ms()
    slept = sleep.counts()
    note = "awake %d turns %d slices %d slept %d sleeps %d refused %d" % (
        _awake + time.ticks_diff(now, _woke), _turns, _slices, (slept[0] - _slept[0]) // 1000,
        slept[1] - _slept[1], slept[2] - _slept[2])
    _awake = _turns = _slices = 0
    _woke = now
    _slept = slept
    return note


def mark_charge():
    global _marked
    if _marked is not None and time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _marked) < MARK_EVERY_MS:
        return
    level = battery.level()
    if level is None:
        return
    _marked = time.ticks_ms()
    screen.charge(*level)


def nap():
    global _awake, _turns, _woke
    _awake += time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _woke)
    _turns += 1
    slumber()
    _woke = time.ticks_ms()


def slumber():
    global _slices
    motor.rest()
    if screen.lit() or touch.busy():
        for _ in range(LIT_NAP_MS // AWAKE_SLICE_MS):
            time.sleep_ms(AWAKE_SLICE_MS)
        return
    for _ in range(DARK_NAP_MS // DARK_SLICE_MS):
        time.sleep_ms(DARK_SLICE_MS)
        _slices += 1
        if touch.busy() or wheel.busy():
            return


def alarm_low():
    global _checked, _alarmed
    if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _checked) < GAUGE_EVERY_MS:
        return
    _checked = time.ticks_ms()
    level = battery.level()
    if level is None or level[0] >= LOW_PERCENT or battery.charging():
        _alarmed = None
        return
    if _alarmed is None or time.ticks_diff(_checked, _alarmed) >= ALARM_EVERY_MS:
        _alarmed = _checked
        screen.say("battery low: %d %%" % level[0])
        motor.buzz()
        speaker.ring()


def tell_charge(watch):
    global _told
    _told = time.ticks_ms()
    level = battery.level()
    if level is None:
        return
    try:
        watch.send_charge("charge %d %% %d mV%s" % (level[0], level[1],
                                                  " charging" if battery.charging() else ""))
    except link.Stalled:
        pass


def bar(wifi_state=None, phone_state=None):
    global _wifi, _phone, _gauged
    _wifi = wifi_state or _wifi
    _phone = phone_state or _phone
    _gauged = time.ticks_ms()
    ram = "%.1fM" % (gc.mem_free() / 1_000_000)
    level = battery.level()
    if level is None:
        screen.button("no battery W B %s" % ram, wifi=_wifi, phone=_phone)
        return
    percent = "%d%%" % level[0]
    screen.button("%s %.2fV W B %s" % (percent, level[1] / 1000, ram),
                  blue=len(percent) if battery.charging() else 0, charge=level[0], wifi=_wifi,
                  phone=_phone)


def glance():
    when = clock.now()
    if when is None:
        screen.clock("--:--")
    else:
        screen.clock("%02d:%02d %s %02d/%02d" % (when[3], when[4], DAYS[when[6]], when[2], when[1]))


def refresh():
    bar()
    glance()


def stamped(when, text):
    year, month, day, hour, minute = when
    now = clock.now()
    if now is not None and tuple(now[:3]) == (year, month, day):
        return "%02d:%02d %s" % (hour, minute, text)
    return "%02d/%02d %02d:%02d %s" % (day, month, hour, minute, text)


def recording(seconds):
    return "rec %d:%02d / %d:%02d, tap to end" % (
        seconds // 60, seconds % 60, RECORD_MAX_S // 60, RECORD_MAX_S % 60)


def record():
    screen.say(recording(0))
    return mic.record(stop=lambda: touch.tap() is not None, max_seconds=RECORD_MAX_S,
                      tick=lambda seconds: screen.redo(recording(seconds)))


def send_voice(watch, voice):
    screen.wake(touchable=False, why="voice")
    screen.say("sending 0 %")
    started = time.ticks_ms()
    try:
        watch.send(voice, progress=lambda percent: screen.redo("sending %d %%" % percent))
    except link.Stalled:
        screen.say("send stalled, kept")
        return False
    # let the last notifications drain before the stack goes down
    time.sleep_ms(500)
    screen.redo("sent in %d s" % (time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), started) // 1000))
    gc.collect()
    return True


def kept_errors():
    try:
        with open(flash.ERRORS) as log:
            return log.read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def keep_error(error):
    trace = io.StringIO()
    sys.print_exception(error, trace)
    kept = (kept_errors() + trace.getvalue())[-ERRORS_KEPT:]
    with open(flash.ERRORS, "w") as log:
        log.write(kept)


def send_errors(watch):
    lines = kept_errors().splitlines()
    if not lines:
        return
    try:
        watch.send_lines(lines)
    except link.Stalled:
        return
    os.remove(flash.ERRORS)
    screen.say("errors sent to the phone")


def chosen_phone():
    try:
        with open(flash.PHONE) as kept:
            return kept.read().strip()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def choose_phone(chosen, seen):
    names = [""] + seen
    chosen = names[(names.index(chosen) + 1) % len(names)]
    with open(flash.PHONE, "w") as kept:
        kept.write(chosen)
    screen.pad_label("actions", 1, chosen or "any phone")
    return chosen


def toggle_wifi(state):
    if state == "off":
        wifi.on()
        bar("joining")
        return "joining", time.ticks_ms()
    wifi.off()
    bar("off")
    return "off", None


def follow_wifi(state, since):
    if state == "joined" and wifi.idle_ms() > WIFI_IDLE_MS:
        return toggle_wifi(state)
    if state != "joining":
        return state, since
    ip = wifi.joined()
    if ip is not None:
        bar("joined")
        screen.say("wifi " + ip)
        return "joined", since
    if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), since) > WIFI_JOIN_MS:
        wifi.off()
        bar("not found")
        return "off", None
    return state, since


try:
    linked = False
    kept = None
    last_recall = None
    ringing = rung = None
    loud = False
    finding = None
    chosen = chosen_phone()
    seen = [chosen] if chosen else []
    screen.pad_label("actions", 1, chosen or "any phone")
    watch = link.Link(bluetooth.BLE())
    watch.advertise()
    screen.say("waiting for the phone")
    wifi_state, wifi_since = "off", None
    refresh()
    while True:
        screen.alive(busy_note)
        mark_charge()
        writes = watch.next_writes()
        if writes:
            screen.heard(writes)
        wifi_state, wifi_since = follow_wifi(wifi_state, wifi_since)
        if watch.phone_ready != linked:
            if watch.phone_ready and watch.phone_name and watch.phone_name not in seen:
                seen.append(watch.phone_name)
            if watch.phone_ready and chosen and watch.phone_name != chosen:
                screen.say("%s refused, %s chosen" % (watch.phone_name or "phone", chosen), light=False)
                watch.drop()
            linked = watch.phone_ready
            bar(phone_state="linked" if linked else "waiting")
            if linked:
                screen.say((watch.phone_name or "phone") + " linked")
                send_errors(watch)
                tell_charge(watch)
                if kept is not None and send_voice(watch, kept):
                    kept = None
            else:
                watch.advertise()
                screen.say("waiting for the phone")
        when = watch.next_time()
        if when is not None:
            clock.set(when)
        if screen.lit():
            glance()
        pieces = watch.next_pieces()
        if pieces is not None:
            screen.picture_rows(pieces)
            continue
        recall = watch.next_recall()
        if recall is not None:
            priority, when, text = recall
            if priority == 0:
                ringing = None
                continue
            if priority == 7:
                screen.media(text)
                continue
            if (when, text) == last_recall:
                continue
            last_recall = when, text
            screen.say(stamped(when, text), light=priority > 1, recall=priority)
            for _ in range(3 if priority == 5 else 1):
                if priority >= 3:
                    motor.buzz()
                if priority >= 4 and priority != CALL:
                    speaker.ring()
            if priority in (CALL, FIND_ME):
                ringing = rung = time.ticks_ms()
                loud = priority == FIND_ME
            continue
        if ringing is not None:
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), ringing) > RING_FOR_MS:
                ringing = None
            elif time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), rung) >= RING_EVERY_MS:
                rung = time.ticks_ms()
                motor.buzz()
                if loud:
                    speaker.ring()
        if watch.next_save():
            screen.say("saved on the phone")
            continue
        if finding is not None and time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), finding) > FIND_FOR_MS:
            finding = None
        if wheel.held():
            if ringing is not None and loud:
                watch.command(WATCH_FOUND)
            ringing = None
            motor.tick()
            screen.seen()
            screen.torch(False)
            screen.picture(False)
            if screen.pad_on() in screen.PAGES:
                screen.pad(None)
            else:
                refresh()
                screen.wake(touchable=True, why="wheel")
                screen.pad("actions")
            continue
        if wheel.pressed():
            refusing = ringing is not None and not loud
            if ringing is not None:
                watch.command(WATCH_FOUND if loud else REFUSE_CALL)
            ringing = None
            if refusing:
                motor.double()
                screen.seen()
                screen.say("refusing the call")
                continue
            waking = finding is None and not (screen.pad_on() or screen.torch_on() or screen.picture_on()
                                              or screen.touchable())
            motor.tick()
            if waking:
                screen.wake(touchable=True, why="wheel")
            screen.seen()
            if waking:
                refresh()
            elif finding is not None:
                finding = None
                watch.command(PHONE_FOUND)
                screen.say("phone found")
            elif screen.pad_on():
                screen.pad(None)
            elif screen.torch_on():
                screen.torch(False)
            elif screen.picture_on():
                screen.picture(False)
            else:
                screen.dark("wheel")
            continue
        tap = touch.tap(dark=not screen.lit())
        if tap is not None:
            motor.tick()
            if not screen.lit():
                screen.wake(why="tap")
            screen.seen()
            if finding is not None:
                finding = None
                watch.command(PHONE_FOUND)
                screen.say("phone found")
                continue
        if tap is None:
            if screen.lit() and time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _gauged) > GAUGE_EVERY_MS:
                refresh()
            alarm_low()
            if linked and _told is not None and time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _told) >= CHARGE_EVERY_MS:
                tell_charge(watch)
            screen.idle()
            nap()
        elif screen.pad_on() == "media":
            if not watch.command(MEDIA_CODES[screen.pad_column(tap[0])]):
                screen.say("phone away, not sent")
        elif screen.pad_on() in screen.PAGES and tap[1] < screen.HOUR_BOTTOM:
            screen.pad("more" if screen.pad_on() == "actions" else "actions")
        elif screen.pad_on() in screen.PAGES and tap[1] < screen.SLIDER_BOTTOM:
            screen.light_at(tap[0])
        elif screen.pad_on() == "more":
            screen.pad(None)
            screen.say("lit 1 min for 10 min" if screen.stay_lit() else "dark after 5 s again")
        elif screen.pad_on() == "actions" and screen.pad_column(tap[0]) == 1:
            chosen = choose_phone(chosen, seen)
            if linked and chosen and watch.phone_name != chosen:
                watch.drop()
        elif screen.pad_on() == "actions":
            column = screen.pad_column(tap[0])
            screen.pad(None)
            if column == 0:
                screen.torch(True)
            elif watch.command(FIND_PHONE):
                finding = time.ticks_ms()
                screen.say("find phone sent, tap when found")
            else:
                screen.say("phone away, not sent")
        elif screen.torch_on():
            screen.torch(False)
        elif screen.picture_on():
            screen.picture(False)
        elif not screen.touchable():
            refresh()
            screen.wake(why="tap")
        elif abs(tap[2]) >= SWIPE_PX:
            screen.browse(int(tap[2] / SWIPE_PX))
        elif tap[1] < screen.HOUR_BOTTOM:
            pass
        elif tap[1] >= screen.BUTTON_TOP:
            wifi_state, wifi_since = toggle_wifi(wifi_state)
        elif tap[1] >= screen.MEDIA_TOP and screen.playing():
            screen.pad("media")
        elif linked:
            voice = record()
            if not send_voice(watch, voice):
                kept = voice
        elif kept is not None:
            screen.say("one already waiting")
        else:
            kept = record()
            screen.say("kept until the phone links")
except Exception as error:
    screen.say("error: " + str(error))
    keep_error(error)
    flash.restart()
how
on the watch, the screen is a 240x240 st7789 on spi, powered by the pmu’s aldo2 and aldo3.
  • why: the pins and rails are those LilyGo’s library gives the t-watch s3; the pmu answers on i2c at 0x34, and each rail is set to 3.3 V before it is switched on.
  • how: the rotation is LilyGo’s, 2, which shows the text upright on the watch.
  • how: spi runs in mode 3 at 20 MHz, as TFT_eSPI talks to the st7789, with no input pin.
    • why: by default spi 1 takes gpio 13, its output, as its input.
  • how: the font is st7789py’s vga2_8x16, 8x16 pixels.
    • how: six of its unused control codes pairs hold 16x16 icons instead, a code its left half, the next its right: 1 and 2 a call, 3 and 4 an SMS, 5 and 6 WhatsApp, 7 and 8 a mail, 14 and 15 ntfy, 16 and 17 a calendar.
      • why: « icones for weol known apps notifs li;e call or sms »
      • how: a glyph is 16 bytes, a row each, its leftmost pixel the high bit, as st7789py reads it.
      • how: each icon is a filled shape, its details cut out.
        • why: « _cons must be filled, to better see them »

def glyph(rows, half):
    return bytes(sum(0x80 >> x for x, pixel in enumerate(row[half * 8:half * 8 + 8]) if pixel == "#")
                 for row in rows)


def draw_into(font):
    drawn = bytearray(font.FONT)
    for code, rows in ICONS.items():
        for half in (0, 1):
            at = (code + half - font.FIRST) * font.HEIGHT
            drawn[at:at + font.HEIGHT] = glyph(rows, half)
    font.FONT = bytes(drawn)


def quarter(rows, half, side):
    drawn = bytearray()
    for y in range(16):
        row = rows[half * 8 + y // 2][side * 8:side * 8 + 8]
        bits = sum(0x8000 >> x for x in range(16) if row[x // 2] == "#")
        drawn += bytes((bits >> 8, bits & 0xFF))
    return bytes(drawn)


class Big:
    WIDTH = 16
    HEIGHT = 16
    FIRST = 0
    LAST = 4 * len(ICONS)
    FONT = b"".join(quarter(ICONS[code], half, side)
                    for code in sorted(ICONS) for half in (0, 1) for side in (0, 1))


def big(code, half):
    at = 4 * sorted(ICONS).index(code) + 2 * half
    return chr(at) + chr(at + 1)
how
each icon is also drawn doubled, 32x32, as four 16x16 glyphs of a font of its own, Big, its top half two glyphs, its bottom half two more; big gives the two codes of a half.
how
on the desk, icons-preview.py draws the doubled ones four times bigger into a png, from Big as the watch takes it, for an eye to check before they go to the watch.

import struct
import sys
import zlib
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "device"))
from glyphs import ICONS, Big, big  # noqa: E402

SCALE = 4
GAP = 8


def png(path, rows):
    height, width = len(rows), len(rows[0])
    raw = b"".join(b"\x00" + bytes(0 if pixel else 255 for pixel in row) for row in rows)
    chunk = lambda kind, data: (struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + kind + data
                                + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(kind + data)))
    path.write_bytes(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0))
                     + chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b"IEND", b""))


def lit(code, y, x):
    at = ord(big(code, y // 16)[x // 16]) * 32 + (y % 16) * 2 + (x % 16) // 8
    return bool(Big.FONT[at] & 0x80 >> x % 8)


rows = []
for y in range(32 * SCALE):
    row = []
    for code in sorted(ICONS):
        row += [lit(code, y // SCALE, x // SCALE) for x in range(32 * SCALE)] + [False] * GAP
    rows.append(row)
png(Path(sys.argv[1]), rows)
what
« é », « à », « ç » and « è » sit at their codes in the pc’s code page 437, and its other glyphs are taken to follow that page too, as vga fonts do10.
how
each character is turned into its glyph’s code as its row is written.
  • why: « make notifs work with french words, like ‘été’ »
how
the top row holds the hour, yellow and centered, redrawn only when it changes.
how
the lines fill the rows between it and the last two: the media row, then the button.
how
the media row shows what the phone plays, magenta and centered as « < title > », empty when nothing plays.
how
a pad fills the screen with tall columns, their names on the hour row: the media one three, blue, green, blue, « back », « play/pause », « skip », the title on the media row; the actions one three, olive, blue and red, « torch », the phone and « find », under the light bar, « 1/2 » after the names; its second page one, orange, « stay lit », « 2/2 »; lines, hour and bar are kept but not drawn, and put back whole when it closes.
  • how: a pad blackens its area first, so a page drawn over another keeps none of its gaps.
  • how: the light bar spans the two rows under the hour row, white up to the light, grey after.
  • how: a tap’s column is the screen asking which of its pad’s columns lies under it.
how
the hour, the media row and the pad’s names are centered by one helper, and whatever covers the lines, torch, pad or picture, is asked of one test.
  • why: « dry: the button, screen, slider etc can be frol a lib ? »
  • why: the hour and media rows never scroll, nor do columns the full height, so the pad draws right wherever the lines stand.
how
the backlight, on gpio 45, goes off 5 s after the last line or wake, and back on at the next; a new button label alone lights nothing, nor a line said not to light it.
  • why: « 5s rather than 10s »
  • how: with the backlight, the panel itself sleeps, and wakes before it lights.
  • why: asleep, it keeps what was drawn and still takes new lines, at a fraction of its current.
  • how: aldo2, the backlight’s own rail, goes off with it and back on before it lights, as LilyGo’s library does at brightness 0; aldo3 keeps the panel and touch fed11.
  • how: when the light goes off, 5 s or a minute while staying lit, is one piece the screen and its fake under test both hold, so the stories time the watch’s own.

DARK_AFTER_MS = 5_000
STAY_LIT_MS = 60_000
STAY_FOR_MS = 600_000
_lit_until = None


def staying():
    return _lit_until is not None and time.ticks_diff(_lit_until, time.ticks_ms()) > 0


def stay_lit():
    global _lit_until
    _lit_until = None if staying() else time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), STAY_FOR_MS)
    return _lit_until is not None


def _due():
    return time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _changed) > (STAY_LIT_MS if staying() else DARK_AFTER_MS)


LIGHT_LOG_BYTES = 4_000
_light_logged = None


def _log_light(what, drew=None):
    global _light_logged
    now = time.ticks_ms()
    since = "" if _light_logged is None else " %d" % time.ticks_diff(now, _light_logged)
    _light_logged = now
    try:
        if os.stat(flash.LIGHT_LOG)[6] > LIGHT_LOG_BYTES:
            os.rename(flash.LIGHT_LOG, flash.LIGHT_LOG + ".old")
    except OSError:
        pass
    with open(flash.LIGHT_LOG, "a") as log:
        log.write("%d %s%s%s\n" % (now, what, since, "" if drew is None else " : " + drew))


ALIVE_EVERY_MS = 300_000
_alive = None


def alive(note=None):
    global _alive
    if _alive is None or time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _alive) >= ALIVE_EVERY_MS:
        _alive = time.ticks_ms()
        _log_light("alive" if note is None else "alive " + note())
        return True
    return False


def heard(writes):
    _log_light("heard " + writes)


def charge(percent, millivolts):
    _log_light("charge %d %d" % (percent, millivolts))
how
each dark and wake is written to the flash’s light log, as its ticks, « dark » or « wake », what caused it, and the ms since the one before; past 4 kB, the log becomes its .old and starts afresh.
  • how: a wake adds, after « : », what it shows: its view, the lines kept and the last one.
  • why: « never work aroud, always fix. If not clear, add logs to improve knowledge »
how
lit, the backlight’s pin is pulsed fast, on the light’s share of the time, 25 % at start; a tap along the actions pad’s light bar sets it there, from its left edge, 2 %, to its right, 100 %.
  • why: « a way to cuange brightness »
  • why: « control with q slider instead in the 1.5s :enu? »
how
a recall’s rows are drawn reversed, black on their color, until the next tap or wheel press.
  • why: « new notif watching phone highlighted, like bold or something »
how
lit, the screen is either touch-sensitive, its bar white and its text black, or read-only; a line lighting a dark screen lights it read-only.
how
read-only, the bar’s color tells the charge, its text grey: blue down to 60 %, green to 40, yellow to 20, orange to 10, red below, white when no battery answers.
how
the bar’s first characters can stand out, as the percent does while charging: blue on the white bar, white on the colored one.
how
the last line can be redone alone, its row only redrawn, as a running timer is.
how
nothing is erased before being drawn: each row is written over itself padded to the full width, a new line redraws only its own row, and the bar only when its label or color changes.
how
when the lines are full, the st7789 scrolls them itself, a row at a time, and the new line is drawn in the row that came free; the hour, the media row and the bar stay fixed.
  • how: rotation 2 writes the frame memory bottom up, its row 239 at the screen’s top: the bar and the media row are the memory’s fixed top, the hour and the 80 rows never shown its fixed bottom.
  • how: the scroll start goes back a row at each new line, so the lines go up the screen.
how
the last 50 lines are kept; browsing older ones scrolls the other way and draws the line that came in at the top; a new line brings the newest back, redrawing them all.
how
once there are more lines than rows, the hour row’s last 2 px show where the rows stand among the kept lines, a blue thumb sized and placed in proportion, redrawn after each move and after the hour.
  • why: that row never scrolls, so the thumb never tears while the lines move.
how
as a torch, the screen is filled white, lit read-only and never darkened by the 5 s; lines, hour and bar are kept but not drawn, and put back whole, read-only, when the torch goes out.
  • how: the torch lights full, whatever the level the screen is set to.
how
as a picture, the screen is filled black, its scroll put back, and each half-row drawn as it comes; lines, hour and bar are kept but not drawn, and put back whole when it closes.
  • why: rows land where the picture says only while the memory is not scrolled.
how
a line wider than the screen is cut at its spaces into rows of 30 columns at most, each kept as a line of its own; a word wider than a row is cut where the row ends.
how
a line holding an icon’s two codes shows the icon doubled, 32x32, at its left edge over its first two rows; the codes are taken out, and the rest, stamp first, is cut into rows of 26 columns beside it, two rows at least.
  • why: « icons shluld be bigger », « taller », « also alçgned w_th text »
  • how: each icon is drawn in its app’s color on black, whatever its line’s: call green, SMS blue, WhatsApp light green, mail red, ntfy teal, calendar orange.
    • why: « icones in color »
  • how: the fake screen writes the icon’s two codes ahead of the first row, two spaces ahead of the others.
how
a recall, phone notifications included, is drawn by its priority, cyan when only shown, yellow when it buzzes, red when it rings; the watch’s own lines are white; each kept line keeps its color, so browsing and redoing it draw it the same.

def _wrap(text, columns):
    rows, row = [], ""
    for word in text.split(" "):
        while len(word) > columns:
            if row:
                rows.append(row)
                row = ""
            rows.append(word[:columns])
            word = word[columns:]
        if row and len(row) + 1 + len(word) > columns:
            rows.append(row)
            row = word
        else:
            row = row + " " + word if row else word
    rows.append(row)
    return rows


ICON_CODES = (1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 16)
ICON_COLUMNS = 4


def _laid(line, columns):
    for code in ICON_CODES:
        pair = chr(code) + chr(code + 1)
        if pair in line:
            rows = _wrap(line.replace(pair, "", 1), columns - ICON_COLUMNS)
            return [(code, half, row) for half, row in enumerate(rows + [""] * (2 - len(rows)))]
    return [(None, 0, row) for row in _wrap(line, columns)]


def _tint(priority):
    return "red" if priority >= 4 else "yellow" if priority == 3 else "cyan"

def _update(register, keep, bits):
    value = _pmu.readfrom_mem(PMU, register, 1)[0] & keep | bits
    _pmu.writeto_mem(PMU, register, bytes((value,)))

    _update(LDO_ONOFF, 0xFF if on else ~ALDO2_ON & 0xFF, ALDO2_ON if on else 0)

    # 3.3 V is (3300 - 500) / 100 steps above the rails' floor
    _update(ALDO2_VOLT, 0xE0, 28)
    _update(ALDO3_VOLT, 0xE0, 28)
    _update(LDO_ONOFF, 0xFF, ALDO2_ON | ALDO3_ON)

# the font's glyphs from 0x80 on, in code page 437's order
CP437 = "ÇüéâäàåçêëèïîìÄÅÉæÆôöòûùÿÖÜ¢£¥₧ƒáíóúñÑªº¿⌐¬½¼¡«»░▒▓│┤╡╢╖╕╣║╗╝╜╛┐└┴┬├─┼╞╟╚╔╩╦╠═╬╧╨╤╥╙╘╒╓╫╪┘┌█▄▌▐▀αßΓπΣσµτΦΘΩδ∞φε∩≡±≥≤⌠⌡÷≈°∙·√ⁿ²■"


def _glyph(char):
    return char if char < "\x80" or char not in CP437 else chr(0x80 + CP437.index(char))


def _full(text, columns=COLUMNS):
    text = text[:columns] + " " * (columns - len(text[:columns]))
    return "".join(_glyph(char) for char in text)


def _wrap(text, columns):
    rows, row = [], ""
    for word in text.split(" "):
        while len(word) > columns:
            if row:
                rows.append(row)
                row = ""
            rows.append(word[:columns])
            word = word[columns:]
        if row and len(row) + 1 + len(word) > columns:
            rows.append(row)
            row = word
        else:
            row = row + " " + word if row else word
    rows.append(row)
    return rows


ICON_CODES = (1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 16)
ICON_COLUMNS = 4

    for code in ICON_CODES:
        pair = chr(code) + chr(code + 1)
        if pair in line:
            rows = _wrap(line.replace(pair, "", 1), columns - ICON_COLUMNS)
            return [(code, half, row) for half, row in enumerate(rows + [""] * (2 - len(rows)))]
    return [(None, 0, row) for row in _wrap(line, columns)]

def _row(row):

        _tft.text(vga2_8x16, _full(text), 0, top, ink, paper)
    else:
        _tft.text(vga2_8x16, _full(" " * ICON_COLUMNS + text), 0, top, ink, paper)
        if half < 2:
            _tft.text(glyphs.Big, glyphs.big(icon, half), 0, top, ICON_INKS[icon], st7789py.BLACK)
    if ruled:
        _tft.hline(0, top, 240, RULE)


def _covered():
    return _torch or _pad or _picture


def _scrollbar():
    if len(_lines) <= ROWS:
        return
    left = _shown() * 240 // len(_lines)
    right = left + max(THUMB_MIN, ROWS * 240 // len(_lines))
    for a, b, color in ((0, left, st7789py.BLACK), (left, right, st7789py.BLUE), (right, 240, st7789py.BLACK)):
        if b > a and not _covered():
            _tft.fill_rect(a, SCROLLBAR_Y, b - a, SCROLLBAR_HEIGHT, color)


CHARGE_COLORS = ((60, st7789py.color565(0, 160, 255)), (40, st7789py.GREEN), (20, st7789py.YELLOW),
                 (10, st7789py.color565(255, 140, 0)), (0, st7789py.RED))
READ_ONLY_TEXT = st7789py.color565(96, 96, 96)
RULE = st7789py.color565(96, 96, 96)


def _charge_color():
    if _charge is None:
        return st7789py.WHITE
    return next(color for floor, color in CHARGE_COLORS if _charge >= floor)


def _bar():
    color = st7789py.WHITE if _touchable else _charge_color()
    ink = st7789py.BLACK if _touchable else READ_ONLY_TEXT
    charging = st7789py.BLUE if _touchable else st7789py.WHITE
    text = _full(_button)
    _tft.text(vga2_8x16, text[:_blue], 0, BUTTON_TOP, charging, color)
    _tft.text(vga2_8x16, text[_blue:], _blue * vga2_8x16.WIDTH, BUTTON_TOP, ink, color)
    for letter, tint in (("W", WIFI_TINTS[_wifi]), ("B", PHONE_TINTS[_phone])):
        at = text.find(" %s " % letter) + 1
        if at:
            ink = READ_ONLY_TEXT if tint == "grey" else getattr(st7789py, tint.upper())
            _tft.text(vga2_8x16, letter, at * vga2_8x16.WIDTH, BUTTON_TOP, ink, st7789py.BLACK)


def _say(line, color, ruled, fresh, icon=None, half=0):
    global _back
    browsed = _back
    _back = 0
    if not browsed and len(_lines) >= ROWS:
        _scroll(1)
    _lines.append((line, color, ruled, fresh, icon, half))
    del _lines[:-HISTORY]
    if _covered():
        return
    for row in range(ROWS) if browsed else (min(len(_lines), ROWS) - 1,):
        _row(row)
    _scrollbar()


def say(line, light=True, recall=0):
    color = getattr(st7789py, _tint(recall).upper()) if recall else st7789py.WHITE
    for at, (icon, half, row) in enumerate(_laid(line, COLUMNS)):
        _say(row, color, recall and at == 0, bool(recall), icon, half)
    if light and not _torch:
        pad(None)
        wake(_touchable and lit())


def seen():
    global _changed
    if lit():
        _changed = time.ticks_ms()
    if not any(line[3] for line in _lines):
        return
    _lines[:] = [line[:3] + (False,) + line[4:] for line in _lines]
    if not _covered():
        for row in range(ROWS):
            _row(row)


def browse(rows):
    global _back
    for _ in range(abs(rows)):
        if rows > 0 and _shown() > 0:
            _back += 1
            _scroll(-1)
            _row(0)
        elif rows < 0 and _back > 0:
            _back -= 1
            _scroll(1)
            _row(ROWS - 1)
    _scrollbar()
    wake(_touchable and lit(), "browse")


def redo(line):
    _lines[-1] = (line,) + _lines[-1][1:]
    if not _back and not _covered():
        _row(min(len(_lines), ROWS) - 1)


def button(label, blue=0, charge=None, wifi="off", phone="waiting"):
    global _button, _blue, _charge, _wifi, _phone
    if (label, blue, charge, wifi, phone) != (_button, _blue, _charge, _wifi, _phone):
        _button, _blue, _charge, _wifi, _phone = label, blue, charge, wifi, phone
        if not (_torch or _pad):
            _bar()


def _hour():
    _tft.text(vga2_8x16, _full(_centered(_clock)), 0, 0, st7789py.YELLOW, st7789py.BLACK)
    _scrollbar()


def clock(text):
    global _clock
    if text != _clock:
        _clock = text
        if not (_torch or _pad):
            _hour()


def _media_row():
    text = "< %s >" % _media if _media else ""
    _tft.text(vga2_8x16, _full(_centered(text)), 0, MEDIA_TOP, st7789py.MAGENTA, st7789py.BLACK)


def media(title):
    global _media
    title = title[:COLUMNS - 4]
    if title != _media:
        _media = title
        if not (_torch or _picture):
            _media_row()


def playing():
    return bool(_media)


def torch(on):
    global _torch
    if on == _torch:
        return
    _torch = on
    if on:
        _close_pad()
        wake(why="torch")
        _tft.fill(st7789py.WHITE)
        return
    _redraw()
    wake(why="torch")


def _redraw():
    _tft.fill(st7789py.BLACK)
    _hour()
    for row in range(ROWS):
        _row(row)
    _scrollbar()
    _media_row()
    _bar()


def torch_on():
    return _torch


def picture(on):
    global _picture
    if on == _picture:
        return
    _picture = on
    if on:
        _close_pad()
        _tft.vscsad(FIXED_BOTTOM)
        _tft.fill_rect(0, PICTURE_TOP, 240, BUTTON_TOP - PICTURE_TOP, st7789py.BLACK)
        _hour()
        _bar()
        wake(why="picture")
        return
    _scroll(0)
    _redraw()
    wake(why="picture")


# the picture's band, between the hour and the bar, its rows counted from the hour's foot
PICTURE_TOP = vga2_8x16.HEIGHT


def picture_rows(pieces):
    picture(True)
    view = memoryview(pieces)
    for at in range(0, len(pieces), 2 + 2 * HALF):
        _tft.blit_buffer(view[at + 2:at + 2 + 2 * HALF], pieces[at + 1] * HALF, PICTURE_TOP + pieces[at],
                         HALF, 1)
    wake(why="picture")


def picture_on():
    return _picture


def _close_pad():
    global _pad
    _pad = None


def pad(name):
    global _pad
    if name == _pad or _torch:
        return
    _pad = name
    if name is None:
        _redraw()
        return
    columns = PADS[name]
    top = SLIDER_BOTTOM if name in PAGES else 0
    width = 240 // len(columns)
    _tft.fill_rect(0, top, 240, 240 - top, st7789py.BLACK)
    for at, (_, color) in enumerate(columns):
        _tft.fill_rect(at * width + 1, top, width - 2, 240 - top, color)
    _pad_labels()
    if name == "media":
        _media_row()
    if name in PAGES:
        _slider()


_relabeled = {}


def _pad_labels():
    columns = PADS[_pad]
    page = PAGES.get(_pad, "")
    width = (COLUMNS - len(page)) // len(columns)
    labels = "".join(_centered(_relabeled.get((_pad, at), label)[:width], width)
                     for at, (label, _) in enumerate(columns))
    _tft.text(vga2_8x16, _full(labels + page), 0, 0, st7789py.WHITE, st7789py.BLACK)


def pad_label(name, column, label):
    _relabeled[(name, column)] = label
    if _pad == name:
        _pad_labels()


def _slider():
    filled = 240 * _light // 100
    _tft.fill_rect(0, HOUR_BOTTOM, filled, SLIDER_BOTTOM - HOUR_BOTTOM, st7789py.WHITE)
    _tft.fill_rect(filled, HOUR_BOTTOM, 240 - filled, SLIDER_BOTTOM - HOUR_BOTTOM, GREY)


def pad_on():
    return _pad


def pad_column(x):
    return x * len(PADS[_pad]) // 240


def _centered(text, columns=COLUMNS):
    left = (columns - len(text)) // 2
    return " " * left + text + " " * (columns - len(text) - left)


def wake(touchable=False, why="line"):
    global _changed, _touchable
    _changed = time.ticks_ms()
    if touchable != _touchable:
        _touchable = touchable
        if not _covered():
            _bar()
    if not lit():
        _log_light("wake " + why, _drew())
        _backlight_rail(True)
        _tft.cs.on()
        _tft.init(_tft.init_cmds)
        _tft.rotation(2)
        _tft.vscrdef(FIXED_BOTTOM, ROWS * vga2_8x16.HEIGHT, MEMORY_ROWS - FIXED_BOTTOM - ROWS * vga2_8x16.HEIGHT)
        _scroll(0)
        _log_light("shown")
    _shine()


def _drew():
    view = "torch" if _torch else "picture" if _picture else _pad or "lines"
    return "%s %d %s" % (view, len(_lines), _lines[-1][0] if _lines else "")


def _shine():
    global _lit
    _lit = True
    _backlight.init(freq=1000, duty_u16=FULL if _torch else FULL * _light // 100)


def light_at(x):
    global _light
    _light = max(LIGHT_MIN, (x + 1) * 100 // 240)
    if _pad in PAGES:
        _slider()
    if lit():
        _shine()


def lit():
    return _lit


def touchable():
    return lit() and _touchable


def dark(why="idle"):
    global _lit
    _log_light("dark " + why)
    _lit = False
    _backlight.duty_u16(0)
    _tft.sleep_mode(True)
    _tft.cs.on()
    _backlight_rail(False)


def idle():
    if lit() and not (_torch or _picture) and _due():
        pad(None)
        dark()
how
under test, the screen is a fake that appends each line to the file the harness names, cut into rows as the screen cuts it, each line redone in place too, and the hour when it changes; the rows of a recall go also to that file’s .recalls twin, as the screen draws them in their own color, each recall opened by a row of dashes where the screen rules its line, and its color’s name to the .tints twin; it starts lit and read-only, or dark when the harness says so; of its button, only whether it shows charging and the colors of its « W » and « B » go, as they change, to the .bar twin; a recall’s first row goes to the .fresh twin as « fresh … », then « seen » once a tap or press clears it; the light level goes to the .light twin.
  • how: the torch writes « torch on » and « torch off » as lines.
  • how: a picture writes « picture on » and « picture off » as lines, and each half-row it draws to the .picture twin, as its row, its half and its first pixel in hex.
  • how: the media row’s title goes, as it changes, to the .media twin as « media … ».
  • how: it darkens as the screen does, 5 s after its last wake, a minute while staying lit, writing « dark » to the .dark twin.

import os
import time

import flash

BUTTON_TOP = 224
MEDIA_TOP = 208
HOUR_BOTTOM = 16
SLIDER_BOTTOM = 48
LIGHT_MIN = 2
COLUMNS = 30
RULE = "-" * COLUMNS
_clock = ""
_light = 25
_fresh = False
_lit = not os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_DARK")
_touchable = False
_torch = False
_changed = time.ticks_ms()
_charging = None
_wifi = None
_phone = None


def _wrap(text, columns):
    rows, row = [], ""
    for word in text.split(" "):
        while len(word) > columns:
            if row:
                rows.append(row)
                row = ""
            rows.append(word[:columns])
            word = word[columns:]
        if row and len(row) + 1 + len(word) > columns:
            rows.append(row)
            row = word
        else:
            row = row + " " + word if row else word
    rows.append(row)
    return rows


ICON_CODES = (1, 3, 5, 7, 14, 16)
ICON_COLUMNS = 4


def _laid(line, columns):
    for code in ICON_CODES:
        pair = chr(code) + chr(code + 1)
        if pair in line:
            rows = _wrap(line.replace(pair, "", 1), columns - ICON_COLUMNS)
            return [(code, half, row) for half, row in enumerate(rows + [""] * (2 - len(rows)))]
    return [(None, 0, row) for row in _wrap(line, columns)]


def _tint(priority):
    return "red" if priority >= 4 else "yellow" if priority == 3 else "cyan"
WIFI_TINTS = {"off": "grey", "joining": "yellow", "joined": "green", "not found": "red"}
PHONE_TINTS = {"waiting": "yellow", "linked": "green"}
DARK_AFTER_MS = 5_000
STAY_LIT_MS = 60_000
STAY_FOR_MS = 600_000
_lit_until = None


def staying():
    return _lit_until is not None and time.ticks_diff(_lit_until, time.ticks_ms()) > 0


def stay_lit():
    global _lit_until
    _lit_until = None if staying() else time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), STAY_FOR_MS)
    return _lit_until is not None


def _due():
    return time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _changed) > (STAY_LIT_MS if staying() else DARK_AFTER_MS)


LIGHT_LOG_BYTES = 4_000
_light_logged = None


def _log_light(what, drew=None):
    global _light_logged
    now = time.ticks_ms()
    since = "" if _light_logged is None else " %d" % time.ticks_diff(now, _light_logged)
    _light_logged = now
    try:
        if os.stat(flash.LIGHT_LOG)[6] > LIGHT_LOG_BYTES:
            os.rename(flash.LIGHT_LOG, flash.LIGHT_LOG + ".old")
    except OSError:
        pass
    with open(flash.LIGHT_LOG, "a") as log:
        log.write("%d %s%s%s\n" % (now, what, since, "" if drew is None else " : " + drew))


ALIVE_EVERY_MS = 300_000
_alive = None


def alive(note=None):
    global _alive
    if _alive is None or time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _alive) >= ALIVE_EVERY_MS:
        _alive = time.ticks_ms()
        _log_light("alive" if note is None else "alive " + note())
        return True
    return False


def heard(writes):
    _log_light("heard " + writes)


def charge(percent, millivolts):
    _log_light("charge %d %d" % (percent, millivolts))


def _logged(line):
    return [("" if icon is None else chr(icon) + chr(icon + 1) if half == 0 else "  ") + row
            for icon, half, row in _laid(line, COLUMNS)]


_said = []


def say(line, light=True, recall=0):
    global _fresh
    rows = _logged(line)
    _said.extend(rows)
    del _said[:-50]
    with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN"), "a") as log:
        for row in rows:
            log.write(row + "\n")
    if recall:
        with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN") + ".recalls", "a") as log:
            log.write(RULE + "\n")
            for row in rows:
                log.write(row + "\n")
        with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN") + ".tints", "a") as log:
            log.write(_tint(recall) + "\n")
        _twin(".fresh", "fresh " + rows[0])
        _fresh = True
    if light and not _torch:
        pad(None)
        wake(_touchable and _lit)


def seen():
    global _fresh, _changed
    if _lit:
        _changed = time.ticks_ms()
    if _fresh:
        _fresh = False
        _twin(".fresh", "seen")


def light_at(x):
    global _light
    _light = max(LIGHT_MIN, (x + 1) * 100 // 240)
    _twin(".light", "light %d%%" % _light)


def _twin(suffix, line):
    with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN") + suffix, "a") as log:
        log.write(line + "\n")


_twin(".light", "light %d%%" % _light)


def button(label, blue=0, charge=None, wifi="off", phone="waiting"):
    global _charging, _wifi, _phone
    if bool(blue) != _charging:
        _charging = bool(blue)
        _bar("charging" if blue else "on battery")
    if wifi != _wifi:
        _wifi = wifi
        _bar("W " + WIFI_TINTS[wifi])
    if phone != _phone:
        _phone = phone
        _bar("B " + PHONE_TINTS[phone])


def _bar(line):
    with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN") + ".bar", "a") as log:
        log.write(line + "\n")


def clock(text):
    global _clock
    if text != _clock:
        _clock = text
        say(text, light=False)


_media = ""


def media(title):
    global _media
    if title != _media:
        _media = title
        _twin(".media", "media " + title)


def playing():
    return bool(_media)


_pad = None
PAD_COLUMNS = {"media": 3, "actions": 3, "more": 1}
PAGES = {"actions": "1/2", "more": "2/2"}


def pad(name):
    global _pad
    if name != _pad and not _torch:
        _pad = name
        _twin(".media", "pad " + (name or "off"))


def pad_on():
    return _pad


def pad_column(x):
    return x * PAD_COLUMNS[_pad] // 240


def pad_label(name, column, label):
    _twin(".label", "%s %d %s" % (name, column, label))


def redo(line):
    say(line, light=False)


def browse(rows):
    wake(_touchable and _lit, "browse")


def wake(touchable=False, why="line"):
    global _lit, _touchable, _changed
    if not _lit:
        _log_light("wake " + why, _drew())
    _lit, _touchable, _changed = True, touchable, time.ticks_ms()


def _drew():
    view = "torch" if _torch else "picture" if _picture else _pad or "lines"
    return "%s %d %s" % (view, len(_said), _said[-1] if _said else "")


def lit():
    return _lit


def touchable():
    return _lit and _touchable


def dark(why="idle"):
    global _lit
    _log_light("dark " + why)
    _lit = False
    _twin(".dark", "dark")


def torch(on):
    global _torch
    if on != _torch:
        if on:
            pad(None)
        _torch = on
        wake(why="torch")
        say("torch on" if on else "torch off")


def torch_on():
    return _torch


_picture = False


def picture(on):
    global _picture
    if on != _picture:
        if on:
            pad(None)
        _picture = on
        wake(why="picture")
        say("picture on" if on else "picture off", light=False)


def picture_rows(pieces):
    picture(True)
    with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_SCREEN") + ".picture", "a") as log:
        for at in range(0, len(pieces), 242):
            log.write("%d,%d,%02x%02x\n" % (pieces[at], pieces[at + 1], pieces[at + 2], pieces[at + 3]))
    wake(why="picture")


def picture_on():
    return _picture


def idle():
    if _lit and not (_torch or _picture) and _due():
        pad(None)
        dark()
