on the watch, the wheel is the pmu’s power key; its short press is the pmu’s interrupt bit 3 of 0x41 to allow and of 0x49 to read, cleared by writing it back12.
  • how: its hold is bit 2 of the same registers, the long press, raised past the pmu’s own irq time.
    • what: untried on the watch: the bit and the time are as XPowersLib names them for the axp2101.
  • how: the pmu pulls gpio 21 low when it raises one of its interrupts; that fall ends the dark nap, and a press logs when the line fell, « wheel down ».
    • why: « wheel wakes after like 4s »: read only between naps, a press waited up to a second.
    • how: so only the presses may pull it: at import, every other interrupt of 0x40 to 0x42 is turned off and all pending ones, 0x48 to 0x4a, cleared.
      • why: with nearly all of them on and some left pending, the line stayed low and never fell.
import time
from machine import I2C, Pin
import flash

PMU = 0x34
INTEN1 = 0x40
INTEN2 = 0x41
INTEN3 = 0x42
INTSTS1 = 0x48
INTSTS2 = 0x49
INTSTS3 = 0x4A
SHORT_PRESS = 0b1000
LONG_PRESS = 0b100

_i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(10), scl=Pin(11), freq=400_000)
for register, allowed in ((INTEN1, 0), (INTEN2, SHORT_PRESS | LONG_PRESS), (INTEN3, 0)):
    _i2c.writeto_mem(PMU, register, bytes((allowed,)))
for register in (INTSTS1, INTSTS2, INTSTS3):
    _i2c.writeto_mem(PMU, register, b"\xff")
_rang = False
_fell = None


def _ring(pin):
    global _rang, _fell
    _rang = True
    _fell = time.ticks_ms()


_int = Pin(21, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP, hold=True)
_int.irq(_ring, Pin.IRQ_FALLING)


def busy():
    return _rang


def _latched(bit):
    global _rang
    _rang = False
    if not _i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, INTSTS2, 1)[0] & bit:
        return False
    _i2c.writeto_mem(PMU, INTSTS2, bytes((bit,)))
    return True


def pressed():
    if not _latched(SHORT_PRESS):
        return False
    with open(flash.LIGHT_LOG, "a") as log:
        log.write("%d wheel down %s\n" % (time.ticks_ms(), _fell))
    return True


def held():
    return _latched(LONG_PRESS)
how
under test, the wheel is a fake reading its presses, a line each, from the file the story names, « press » or « long », in order; never pressed when it names none. 
import os

_played = 0


def _next(kind):
    global _played
    try:
        with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_WHEEL")) as log:
            presses = log.read().split()
    except (OSError, TypeError):
        return False
    if _played == len(presses) or presses[_played] != kind:
        return False
    _played += 1
    return True


def busy():
    try:
        with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_WHEEL")) as log:
            return len(log.read().split()) > _played
    except (OSError, TypeError):
        return False


def pressed():
    return _next("press")


def held():
    return _next("long")
how
on the watch, the battery’s percent and voltage are the pmu’s own readings, as XPowersLib takes them13; none when no cell is there.
  • how: the pmu’s voltage measure is switched on once, at import.
  • how: the battery is charging when the top bits of the pmu’s second status register say so, as XPowersLib reads it14.

from machine import I2C, Pin

PMU = 0x34
STATUS1 = 0x00
STATUS2 = 0x01
CHARGING = 0b01
ADC_CHANNEL_CTRL = 0x30
BATTERY_MV = 0x34
BATTERY_PERCENT = 0xA4
CELL_THERE = 0b1000

_i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(10), scl=Pin(11), freq=400_000)
_i2c.writeto_mem(PMU, ADC_CHANNEL_CTRL, bytes((_i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, ADC_CHANNEL_CTRL, 1)[0] | 1,)))


def level():
    if not _i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, STATUS1, 1)[0] & CELL_THERE:
        return None
    high, low = _i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, BATTERY_MV, 2)
    return _i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, BATTERY_PERCENT, 1)[0], (high & 0x1F) << 8 | low


def charging():
    return _i2c.readfrom_mem(PMU, STATUS2, 1)[0] >> 5 == CHARGING

on the watch, the chip’s light sleep is read from esp32.pm_dump(): the µs spent in its « SLEEP » mode, the largest number on that row, and the light sleeps made and refused.

import esp32


def counts():
    slept = sleeps = refused = 0
    for line in esp32.pm_dump().splitlines():
        words = line.split()
        if words[:1] == ["SLEEP"]:
            slept = max(int(word) for word in words if word.isdigit())
        elif line.startswith("light_sleep_counts:"):
            sleeps, refused = (int(word.split(":")[1]) for word in words)
    return slept, sleeps, refused

on the watch, a ring is half a second of a 2.7 kHz tone at full scale through the MAX98357A, bck on gpio 48, ws on 15 and data on 46.
  • why: « find my watch wprks but speaker sound is low »: 880 Hz at a quarter of full scale was; so small a speaker is loudest in the kHz, and the amplifier’s gain is set by the board.
  • why: those are the pins LilyGo’s library gives the t-watch s315.
  • how: the amplifier is powered by the pmu’s dldo1, switched on as LilyGo’s library does16.
    • how: only for the ring: dldo1 goes on before the tone and off after it.
    • why: an amplifier left powered draws its idle current all day for a half-second ring now and then.
  • how: the tone is waited out before the amplifier is freed.
import math
import struct
import time
from machine import I2C, I2S, Pin

PMU = 0x34
LDO_ONOFF = 0x90
DLDO1_ON = 0b10000000
RATE = 16000

_pmu = I2C(0, sda=Pin(10), scl=Pin(11), freq=400_000)


def _powered(on):
    value = _pmu.readfrom_mem(PMU, LDO_ONOFF, 1)[0]
    _pmu.writeto_mem(PMU, LDO_ONOFF, bytes((value | DLDO1_ON if on else value & ~DLDO1_ON,)))


_powered(False)


def ring(ms=500, hz=2700):
    count = RATE * ms // 1000
    tone = bytearray(2 * count)
    for n in range(count):
        struct.pack_into("<h", tone, 2 * n, int(32000 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * hz * n / RATE)))
    _powered(True)
    amp = I2S(1, sck=Pin(48), ws=Pin(15), sd=Pin(46), mode=I2S.TX,
              bits=16, format=I2S.MONO, rate=RATE, ibuf=len(tone))
    amp.write(tone)
    time.sleep_ms(ms)
    amp.deinit()
    _powered(False)

on the watch, a buzz is the drv2605’s 750 ms alert, effect 1517, on its erm motor, as LilyGo’s library plays it at start16.
  • how: the drv2605 answers on the pmu’s i2c at 0x5A17, powered by the pmu’s bldo2 at 3.3 V.
    • how: only for the buzz: bldo2 goes on, the drv2605 is set up afresh, the alert is waited out, and bldo2 goes off.
    • why: as with the amplifier, a rail left on feeds the drv2605 all day for a rare buzz.
  • how: a tick is the same, with the strong buzz, effect 1417, lasting 150 ms.
    • how: it is not waited out: the drv2605 plays alone, and bldo2 goes off on the main loop’s next nap once the 150 ms are past.
      • why: « shpuld vibrate when gettçnf the tap/press, not when lighton the screen »: the tick comes first, the screen waking while it plays.
    • why: « tap and wheel vibrarion must be more noticeable »: the strong click, effect 1, was missed.
how
a double buzz is the alert twice, 200 ms apart, in one sequence: a wait step is 0x80 plus tens of ms17.

import time
from machine import I2C, Pin

PMU = 0x34
LDO_ONOFF = 0x90
BLDO2_VOLT = 0x97
BLDO2_ON = 0b100000
DRV = 0x5A
MODE, LIBRARY, SEQUENCE, GO, FEEDBACK = 0x01, 0x03, 0x04, 0x0C, 0x1A
ALERT, ALERT_MS = 15, 750
CLICK, CLICK_MS = 14, 150
WAIT, GAP_MS = 0x80, 200

_i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(10), scl=Pin(11), freq=400_000)


def _update(device, register, keep, bits):
    value = _i2c.readfrom_mem(device, register, 1)[0] & keep | bits
    _i2c.writeto_mem(device, register, bytes((value,)))


_update(PMU, BLDO2_VOLT, 0xE0, 28)
_update(PMU, LDO_ONOFF, ~BLDO2_ON & 0xFF, 0)


_resting = None


def _start(effects):
    _update(PMU, LDO_ONOFF, 0xFF, BLDO2_ON)
    # internal trigger, out of standby, erm library a, erm feedback
    _update(DRV, MODE, 0x00, 0x00)
    _update(DRV, LIBRARY, 0xF8, 1)
    _update(DRV, FEEDBACK, 0x7F, 0)
    _i2c.writeto_mem(DRV, SEQUENCE, bytes(effects + (0,)))
    _i2c.writeto_mem(DRV, GO, b"\x01")


def _off():
    global _resting
    _resting = None
    _update(PMU, LDO_ONOFF, ~BLDO2_ON & 0xFF, 0)


def _play(effects, ms):
    _start(effects)
    time.sleep_ms(ms)
    _off()


def rest():
    if _resting is not None and time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), _resting) >= 0:
        _off()


def buzz():
    _play((ALERT,), ALERT_MS)


def double():
    _play((ALERT, WAIT | GAP_MS // 10, ALERT), 2 * ALERT_MS + GAP_MS)


def tick():
    global _resting
    _start((CLICK,))
    _resting = time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), CLICK_MS)

on the watch, the microphone is the pdm one, clock on gpio 44 and data on gpio 47, read through the patched machine.I2S into a 16 kHz, 16-bit, mono wav.
  • why: those are the pins the circuitpython board names; the vendor powers no rail for it, so it hangs on the always-on 3.3 V.
  • why: the patched pdm reception gives half the rate it is asked for, 8004 samples a second for 16000 asked, so it is asked twice the rate wanted.
  • why: the mic is quiet and sits on an offset, speech peaking near 3500 over about -1500, so the offset is taken away and the rest made 8 times louder.
  • how: it records until stop says so, looked at each tenth of a second, or until the cap, 3 s by default; tick hears each whole second recorded.
  • how: the wav is made in one buffer, its header written last, the sound made louder in place by viper code, so a long recording is never copied.
  • how: that buffer, room for 2 min, is taken once at import and each recording reuses it; the next recording overwrites the last.
    • why: taken afresh each time, a few recordings cut the heap up until the next could not fit.
    • why: the watch holds the whole recording before sending it; two copies of a 2 min one would not fit its 8 MB.
import struct

import micropython
from machine import I2S, Pin

RATE = 16000
GAIN = 8
HEADER = 44
SLICE = RATE * 2 // 10
SUM_CHUNK = 32768
MAX_SECONDS = 120
_wav = bytearray(HEADER + RATE * 2 * MAX_SECONDS)


def wav_header(size):
    return (b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", 36 + size) + b"WAVEfmt "
​            + struct.pack("<IHHIIHH", 16, 1, 1, RATE, RATE * 2, 2, 16)
​            + b"data" + struct.pack("<I", size))


@micropython.viper
def _sum(samples: ptr16, count: int) -> int:
    total = 0
    for i in range(count):
        value = int(samples[i])
        if value > 32767:
            value -= 65536
        total += value
    return total


@micropython.viper
def _louder(samples: ptr16, count: int, offset: int, gain: int):
    for i in range(count):
        value = int(samples[i])
        if value > 32767:
            value -= 65536
        value = (value - offset) * gain
        if value > 32767:
            value = 32767
        if value < -32768:
            value = -32768
        samples[i] = value & 0xFFFF


def louder(pcm):
    count = len(pcm) // 2
    total = 0
    for start in range(0, count, SUM_CHUNK):
        total += _sum(pcm[2 * start:], min(SUM_CHUNK, count - start))
    _louder(pcm, count, total // count, GAIN)


def record(stop=None, max_seconds=3, tick=None):
    mic = I2S(0, sck=Pin(44), sd=Pin(47), mode=I2S.PDM_RX,
              bits=16, format=I2S.MONO, rate=2 * RATE, ibuf=20000)
    end = HEADER + RATE * 2 * min(max_seconds, MAX_SECONDS)
    view = memoryview(_wav)
    got = 0
    second = 0
    while HEADER + got < end:
        got += mic.readinto(view[HEADER + got:min(HEADER + got + SLICE, end)])
        if stop is not None and stop():
            break
        if tick is not None and got // (RATE * 2) != second:
            second = got // (RATE * 2)
            tick(second)
    mic.deinit()
    got -= got % 2
    louder(view[HEADER:HEADER + got])
    view[:HEADER] = wav_header(got)
    return view[:HEADER + got]

the mic is tried alone on the watch, with no desktop: at boot, each tap on the screen records 3 s, shows how loud it was, and keeps the wav on the watch’s flash.
  • why: a mute or deaf mic shows at once in its loudness, before ble adds its own doubts.
  • how: the touch panel is an ft6336 at 0x38 on its own i2c, sda 39 and scl 40, powered with the screen by aldo3; its register 2 counts the fingers on it, and registers 3 to 6 hold the first finger’s x and y on 12 bits.
  • how: a tap is told on release, at where the finger last was, with how far it went down since it touched; the panel’s coordinates are the screen’s as drawn.
  • how: the panel pulls gpio 16 low when a finger lands; only from then until the release is it read, so the i2c rests while nothing touches.
    • how: a fall with no finger seen down is no tap: only a finger the panel reported down makes one.
      • why: « watch is flashong now. lit, dark, lit, dark etc… »: with the chip light-sleeping, gpio 16 falls by itself, and each fall made a tap, a tick and a lit screen about 3 times a second.
      • what: a tap lifted before the next look is lost, save on a dark screen, where it still wakes it.
        • why: « a lot of taps just don’t wake the watch »; gpio 16, held up through sleep, no longer falls by itself.

import time
from machine import I2C, Pin
import flash

PANEL = 0x38
FINGERS = 0x02
FIRST_XH = 0x03
_i2c = I2C(1, sda=Pin(39), scl=Pin(40), freq=400_000)
_first = None
_last = None
_landed = False


def _land(pin):
    global _landed
    _landed = True


_int = Pin(16, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP, hold=True)
_int.irq(_land, Pin.IRQ_FALLING)


def touched():
    return _i2c.readfrom_mem(PANEL, FINGERS, 1)[0] & 0x0F > 0


def wait_tap():
    while not touched():
        time.sleep_ms(20)
    while touched():
        time.sleep_ms(20)


def _where():
    xh, xl, yh, yl = _i2c.readfrom_mem(PANEL, FIRST_XH, 4)
    return (xh & 0x0F) << 8 | xl, (yh & 0x0F) << 8 | yl


def busy():
    return _landed or _last is not None


def _log(what):
    with open(flash.LIGHT_LOG, "a") as log:
        log.write("%d %s\n" % (time.ticks_ms(), what))


def tap(dark=False):
    global _first, _last, _landed
    if not _landed and _last is None:
        return None
    _landed = False
    if touched():
        if _first is None:
            _log("touch down")
        _last = _where()
        _first = _first or _last
        return None
    if _last is None:
        _log("touch lost")
        return (0, 0, 0) if dark else None
    (x, y), (_, y0) = _last, _first
    _first = _last = None
    _log("touch up")
    return x, y, y - y0
how
under test, the touch is a fake playing, one per look, the taps the story adds as x,y lines to the file the harness names; none moves; a « lost » line is a tap lifted before the look.
import os

_played = 0


def _taps():
    try:
        with open(os.getenv("TWATCH_FAKE_TAPS")) as log:
            return log.read().split()
    except OSError:
        return []


def busy():
    return len(_taps()) > _played


def tap(dark=False):
    global _played
    taps = _taps()
    if _played == len(taps):
        return None
    _played += 1
    if taps[_played - 1] == "lost":
        return (0, 0, 0) if dark else None
    x, y = taps[_played - 1].split(",")
    return int(x), int(y), 0

import array
import os

def save(wav):

how
the watch serves one service: the phone writes READY, its name in at most 20 bytes of utf-8, or a single byte below a space when it gives none, and the voice comes back as notifications on VOICE; a recall is written on RECALL, its priority on one byte, then when it was sent, year on two bytes, month, day, hour and minute on one each, then its text; SAVED is written once the phone has saved a recording; the REPL’s input is written on REPL_IN, its output notified on REPL_OUT; the phone’s local time is written on TIME as year on two bytes, then month, day, weekday from monday as 0, hour, minute and second on one each; a media command goes out as a notification on MEDIA, one byte: 1 back, 2 play or pause, 3 skip; each line of the errors kept goes out as a notification on ERRORS, cut to a packet; the charge goes out the same way on CHARGE. 
import bluetooth
import struct
import time
from micropython import const

import repl

_IRQ_CENTRAL_CONNECT = const(1)
_IRQ_CENTRAL_DISCONNECT = const(2)
_IRQ_GATTS_WRITE = const(3)
_IRQ_MTU_EXCHANGED = const(21)

NAME = "twatch"
SERVICE = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0001-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
VOICE = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0002-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
READY = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0003-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
RECALL = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0004-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
SAVED = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0005-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
REPL_IN = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0006-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
REPL_OUT = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0007-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
TIME = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0008-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
MEDIA = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-0009-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
PICTURE = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-000a-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
ERRORS = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-000c-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
CHARGE = bluetooth.UUID("8d5a7819-000d-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
PIECE = 242
PROGRESS_STEP = 5
STALL_MS = 10_000
CALL_US = 1_340_000


class Stalled(Exception):
    pass


def phone_name(written):
    if written[:1] < b" ":
        return ""
    try:
        return written.decode()
    except UnicodeError:
        return ""
how
the link is one class, whose methods the bullets below carve out.
how
the link remembers who is connected, whether the phone is ready, how big a packet may be, and the recalls not yet shown.
  • how: a recall’s characteristic holds a full packet, 244 bytes, where micropython gives 20 by default and would cut its text.

def __init__(self, ble):
    self.ble = ble
    ble.active(True)
    ble.config(gap_name=NAME, mtu=247)
    ((self.voice, self.ready, self.recall, self.saved, self.repl_in, self.repl_out, self.clock,
      self.media, self.picture, self.errors, self.charge),) = (
        ble.gatts_register_services(
            ((SERVICE, ((VOICE, bluetooth.FLAG_NOTIFY), (READY, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE),
                        (RECALL, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE), (SAVED, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE),
                        (REPL_IN, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE), (REPL_OUT, bluetooth.FLAG_NOTIFY),
                        (TIME, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE), (MEDIA, bluetooth.FLAG_NOTIFY),
                        (PICTURE, bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE | bluetooth.FLAG_WRITE_NO_RESPONSE),
                        (ERRORS, bluetooth.FLAG_NOTIFY), (CHARGE, bluetooth.FLAG_NOTIFY))),)))
    ble.gatts_set_buffer(self.repl_in, 512)
    ble.gatts_set_buffer(self.recall, 244)
    ble.gatts_set_buffer(self.picture, 2 * PIECE, True)
    self.names = {self.ready: "ready", self.recall: "recall", self.saved: "saved", self.repl_in: "repl",
                  self.clock: "time", self.picture: "picture"}
    self.writes = {}
    self.pieces = bytearray()
    self.conn = None
    self.mtu = 23
    self.phone_ready = False
    self.phone_name = ""
    self.recalls = []
    self.saves = 0
    self.time = None
    self.repl = None
    ble.irq(self._irq)

def _irq(self, event, data):
    if event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE:
        name = self.names.get(data[1], "?")
        self.writes[name] = self.writes.get(name, 0) + 1
    if event == _IRQ_CENTRAL_CONNECT:
        self.conn = data[0]
    elif event == _IRQ_CENTRAL_DISCONNECT:
        self.conn = None
        self.phone_ready = False
        self.advertise()
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.ready:
        self.phone_name = phone_name(bytes(self.ble.gatts_read(self.ready)))
        self.phone_ready = True
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.recall:
        written = self.ble.gatts_read(self.recall)
        priority, *when = struct.unpack_from("<BHBBBB", written)
        self.recalls.append((priority, when, bytes(written[7:]).decode()))
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.saved:
        self.saves += 1
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.clock:
        self.time = struct.unpack("<HBBBBBB", self.ble.gatts_read(self.clock))
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.repl_in:
        if self.repl is None:
            self.repl = repl.Stream(self)
        self.repl.received(self.ble.gatts_read(self.repl_in))
    elif event == _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE and data[1] == self.picture:
        self.pieces += self.ble.gatts_read(self.picture)
    elif event == _IRQ_MTU_EXCHANGED:
        self.mtu = data[1]
how
the watch advertises its name every 1.34 s, until a phone links, and again as soon as any link drops, ready or not.
  • what: each of the four Android scans the pace story names hears this beat within 30 s, from any start.
  • what: it costs 3.7 times the calls of a 5 s beat, only while unlinked.

def advertise(self):
    name = NAME.encode()
    adv = bytes((2, 0x01, 0x06, len(name) + 1, 0x09)) + name
    self.ble.gap_advertise(CALL_US, adv_data=adv)

def drop(self):
    self.phone_ready = False
    if self.conn is not None:
        self.ble.gap_disconnect(self.conn)
how
a recording goes out as its length on four bytes, then its bytes, cut to the packet size, sent from where it lies rather than copied behind its length; each 5 % sent is told to whoever asks.
  • how: a packet waits while the controller’s buffers are full; after 10 s without one going out, the link is dropped and the send fails, as it does when the phone leaves mid-way.

def send(self, payload, progress=None):
    step = self.mtu - 3
    view = memoryview(payload)
    told = 0
    self._notify(struct.pack("<I", len(payload)) + bytes(view[:step - 4]))
    for offset in range(step - 4, len(payload), step):
        self._notify(view[offset:offset + step])
        percent = offset * 100 // len(payload) // PROGRESS_STEP * PROGRESS_STEP
        if progress is not None and percent != told:
            told = percent
            progress(percent)

def send_lines(self, lines):
    for line in lines:
        self._notify(line.encode()[:self.mtu - 3], self.errors)

def send_charge(self, line):
    self._notify(line.encode()[:self.mtu - 3], self.charge)

def _notify(self, chunk, handle=None):
    since = time.ticks_ms()
    while self.conn is not None:
        try:
            self.ble.gatts_notify(self.conn, handle or self.voice, chunk)
            return
        except OSError:
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), since) > STALL_MS:
                self.ble.gap_disconnect(self.conn)
                break
            time.sleep_ms(2)
    raise Stalled()
how
the recalls come out in the order they came in, none when none waits; so do the phone’s word that a recording is saved, and the last time it gave.
how
a media command goes only while linked; unlinked, or stalled, it is lost and said so.
how
what the phone writes on PICTURE piles up, and comes out as whole half-rows of 242 bytes.
  • why: micropython reads a written value only once its irq runs; piling them, none is lost.

def next_recall(self):
    return self.recalls.pop(0) if self.recalls else None

def next_writes(self):
    writes, self.writes = self.writes, {}
    return " ".join("%s %d" % pair for pair in sorted(writes.items()))

def next_save(self):
    if not self.saves:
        return False
    self.saves -= 1
    return True

def next_time(self):
    when, self.time = self.time, None
    return when

def next_pieces(self):
    whole = len(self.pieces) - len(self.pieces) % PIECE
    if not whole:
        return None
    pieces, self.pieces = self.pieces[:whole], self.pieces[whole:]
    return pieces

def command(self, code):
    if self.conn is None:
        return False
    try:
        self._notify(bytes((code,)), self.media)
    except Stalled:
        return False
    return True
how
the REPL also runs over the phone’s link, as micropython’s ble_uart_repl example does: what the phone writes on REPL_IN is fed to os.dupterm, and what the REPL prints goes back on REPL_OUT, cut to the packet size.
  • how: the stream takes the REPL each time the phone writes, so the wifi’s REPL and this one share micropython’s one hook: the last to write is served; the usb REPL is apart.
import io
import os

import micropython
from micropython import const

_MP_STREAM_POLL = const(3)
_MP_STREAM_POLL_RD = const(1)


class Stream(io.IOBase):
    def __init__(self, link):
        self.link = link
        self.inbox = bytearray()
        self.outbox = bytearray()

    def received(self, data):
        self.inbox += data
        os.dupterm(self)
        os.dupterm_notify(None)

    def readinto(self, buf):
        if not self.inbox:
            return None
        count = min(len(buf), len(self.inbox))
        buf[:count] = self.inbox[:count]
        self.inbox = self.inbox[count:]
        return count

    def ioctl(self, op, arg):
        if op == _MP_STREAM_POLL and self.inbox:
            return _MP_STREAM_POLL_RD
        return 0

    def write(self, buf):
        idle = not self.outbox
        self.outbox += buf
        if idle:
            micropython.schedule(self._flush, None)
        return len(buf)

    def _flush(self, _):
        step = self.link.mtu - 3
        chunk, self.outbox = self.outbox[:step], self.outbox[step:]
        try:
            self.link._notify(chunk, self.link.repl_out)
        except Exception:
            self.outbox = bytearray()
        if self.outbox:
            micropython.schedule(self._flush, None)

the voice, on the phone

what
the phone finds the watch, takes one recording, saves it in the inbox, and tells the watch.
  • scope: under test it runs on the desktop, on bumble; on the phone, the ble stack will differ.
import asyncio
import contextlib
import struct
import time

from bumble.core import UUID, AdvertisingData
from bumble.device import Device, Peer
from bumble.hci import Address
from bumble.transport import open_transport

NAME = "twatch"
SERVICE = UUID("8d5a7819-0001-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
VOICE = UUID("8d5a7819-0002-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
READY = UUID("8d5a7819-0003-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
RECALL = UUID("8d5a7819-0004-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
SAVED = UUID("8d5a7819-0005-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
TIME = UUID("8d5a7819-0008-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
MEDIA = UUID("8d5a7819-0009-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
PICTURE = UUID("8d5a7819-000a-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
ERRORS = UUID("8d5a7819-000c-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")
CHARGE = UUID("8d5a7819-000d-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01")


async def receive_one(transport, inbox):
    async with linked(transport) as peer:
        recording = await receive_recording(peer)
        inbox.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = inbox / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S.wav")
        path.write_bytes(recording)
        saved = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(SAVED, SERVICE)[0]
        await peer.write_value(saved, b"\x01", with_response=True)
    return path
how
the phone stays linked to the watch while the story needs it, and unlinks on leaving; once linked, it learns the watch’s service. 
@contextlib.asynccontextmanager
async def linked(transport):
    async with await open_transport(transport) as hci:
        device = Device.with_hci("phone", Address("F0:F1:F2:F3:F4:F5"), hci.source, hci.sink)
        await device.power_on()
        connection = await device.connect(await find_watch(device))
        gone = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        connection.on("disconnection", lambda reason: gone.done() or gone.set_result(reason))
        try:
            peer = Peer(connection)
            peer.gone = gone
            await peer.discover_services([SERVICE])
            await peer.discover_characteristics()
            yield peer
        finally:
            if not gone.done():
                await connection.disconnect()
how
the watch is the first device advertising its name. 
async def find_watch(device):
    found = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()

    def on_advertisement(advertisement):
        name = advertisement.data.get(AdvertisingData.Type.COMPLETE_LOCAL_NAME)
        if name == NAME and not found.done():
            found.set_result(advertisement.address)

    device.on("advertisement", on_advertisement)
    await device.start_scanning()
    address = await found
    await device.stop_scanning()
    return address
how
the phone asks for packets of 24 bytes, listens on VOICE, then says READY with its name, « phone »; the recording is whole once the announced length has arrived. 
async def receive_recording(peer):
    await peer.request_mtu(24)
    voice = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(VOICE, SERVICE)[0]
    ready = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(READY, SERVICE)[0]
    received = bytearray()
    complete = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()

    def on_chunk(chunk):
        received.extend(chunk)
        if len(received) >= 4:
            (length,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", received)
            if len(received) - 4 >= length and not complete.done():
                complete.set_result(bytes(received[4:4 + length]))

    await peer.subscribe(voice, on_chunk)
    await peer.write_value(ready, b"phone", with_response=True)
    return await complete
how
the phone listens on ERRORS, or CHARGE, before it says READY, and gathers the lines the watch sends there until one holds what it waits for. 
async def receive_errors(peer, until):
    return await receive_lines(peer, ERRORS, until)


async def receive_charge(peer, until):
    return await receive_lines(peer, CHARGE, until)


async def receive_lines(peer, uuid, until):
    await peer.request_mtu(247)
    channel = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(uuid, SERVICE)[0]
    ready = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(READY, SERVICE)[0]
    lines = []
    heard = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()

    def on_line(value):
        lines.append(bytes(value).decode())
        if until in lines[-1] and not heard.done():
            heard.set_result(lines)

    await peer.subscribe(channel, on_line)
    await peer.write_value(ready, b"phone", with_response=True)
    return await asyncio.wait_for(heard, 10)
how
the phone says READY with the name it is told. 
async def say_ready(peer, name):
    ready = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(READY, SERVICE)[0]
    await peer.write_value(ready, name.encode(), with_response=True)
how
a recall is its priority, 3 unless told, when it was sent, now unless told, then its text, written on RECALL. 
async def send_recall(peer, text, priority=3, when=None):
    recall = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(RECALL, SERVICE)[0]
    stamp = struct.pack("<BHBBBB", priority, *(when or time.localtime()[:5]))
    await peer.write_value(recall, stamp + text.encode(), with_response=True)
how
a picture is 240x208 pixels, the band between the hour and the bar, 16 bits each, big-endian, red 5, green 6, blue 5, as the st7789 takes them; it goes as 416 half-rows on PICTURE, each its row, its half, 0 left or 1 right, then its 120 pixels, 242 bytes, so packets of 247 bytes are asked first. 
async def send_picture(peer, pixels):
    await peer.request_mtu(247)
    picture = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(PICTURE, SERVICE)[0]
    for y in range(208):
        for half in (0, 1):
            at = (y * 240 + half * 120) * 2
            await peer.write_value(picture, bytes((y, half)) + pixels[at:at + 240], with_response=True)
how
the phone hears each media command the watch notifies on MEDIA, a single byte: 1 back, 2 play or pause, 3 skip, 9 ring the phone, 10 found, 11 watch found, 12 refuse the ringing call. 
async def hear_media(peer, heard):
    media = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(MEDIA, SERVICE)[0]
    await peer.subscribe(media, lambda value: heard(value[0]))
how
a notification is a recall whose text is its app, its title and its text, one after the other.
  • how: ntfy’s go without the app’s name, and a title that is only the server and the topic, as « 192.168.2.14:9705/n », shrinks to the topic.
    • why: that address and « ntfy » took a whole row before the message began.
  • how: a time opening the text goes, as the stamp already says it; a link shrinks to its host, a date and time to its hour and minute, and what the watch’s font cannot draw, as emoji, goes.
    • how: a letter the font lacks loses its accent, « ō » becoming « o », and « œ » is spelled « oe ».
    • why: the screen is 30 columns; a grafana link alone filled some 30 rows.
  • how: a known app’s icon takes the place of its name: Signal, SMS and mail apps by their package, any call or mail by its category; other apps keep their name.

import re
import unicodedata

NTFY_ADDRESS = re.compile(r"^[\w.-]+(:\d+)?/([\w-]+)$")
LEADING_TIME = re.compile(r"^\d\d:\d\d: ?")
LINK = re.compile(r"https?://([^/\s]+)\S*")
DATE_TIME = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d[ T](\d\d:\d\d)(:\d\d(\.\d+)?)?")


def plain(text):
    text = DATE_TIME.sub(r"\1", LINK.sub(r"\1", text))
    return " ".join("".join(_drawable(char) for char in text).split())


SPELLED = {"œ": "oe", "Œ": "OE"}


def _drawable(char):
    try:
        char.encode("cp437")
        return char
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return SPELLED.get(char) or unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", char).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()


CALL_ICON, SMS_ICON, WHATSAPP_ICON, MAIL_ICON = "\x01\x02", "\x03\x04", "\x05\x06", "\x07\x08"
NTFY_ICON, CALENDAR_ICON = "\x0e\x0f", "\x10\x11"
PACKAGE_ICONS = {
    "com.whatsapp": WHATSAPP_ICON,
    "io.heckel.ntfy": NTFY_ICON,
    "com.google.android.apps.messaging": SMS_ICON,
    "com.android.messaging": SMS_ICON,
    "com.android.mms": SMS_ICON,
    "com.google.android.gm": MAIL_ICON,
    "com.fsck.k9": MAIL_ICON,
    "eu.faircode.email": MAIL_ICON,
}
CATEGORY_ICONS = {"call": CALL_ICON, "email": MAIL_ICON, "event": CALENDAR_ICON, "reminder": CALENDAR_ICON}


def icon(package, category):
    return PACKAGE_ICONS.get(package) or CATEGORY_ICONS.get(category)


def worded(app, title, text, package=None, category=None):
    text = LEADING_TIME.sub("", text or "")
    if app == "ntfy":
        address = NTFY_ADDRESS.match(title or "")
        title = address.group(2) if address else title
        return NTFY_ICON + plain("{}: {}".format(title, text) if title else text)
    known = icon(package, category)
    if known:
        return known + plain("{}: {}".format(title or "", text))
    return plain("{}: {}: {}".format(app, title or "", text))

import re
import unicodedata

NTFY_ADDRESS = re.compile(r"^[\w.-]+(:\d+)?/([\w-]+)$")
LEADING_TIME = re.compile(r"^\d\d:\d\d: ?")
LINK = re.compile(r"https?://([^/\s]+)\S*")
DATE_TIME = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d[ T](\d\d:\d\d)(:\d\d(\.\d+)?)?")


def plain(text):
    text = DATE_TIME.sub(r"\1", LINK.sub(r"\1", text))
    return " ".join("".join(_drawable(char) for char in text).split())


SPELLED = {"œ": "oe", "Œ": "OE"}


def _drawable(char):
    try:
        char.encode("cp437")
        return char
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return SPELLED.get(char) or unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", char).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()


CALL_ICON, SMS_ICON, WHATSAPP_ICON, MAIL_ICON = "\x01\x02", "\x03\x04", "\x05\x06", "\x07\x08"
NTFY_ICON, CALENDAR_ICON = "\x0e\x0f", "\x10\x11"
PACKAGE_ICONS = {
    "com.whatsapp": WHATSAPP_ICON,
    "io.heckel.ntfy": NTFY_ICON,
    "com.google.android.apps.messaging": SMS_ICON,
    "com.android.messaging": SMS_ICON,
    "com.android.mms": SMS_ICON,
    "com.google.android.gm": MAIL_ICON,
    "com.fsck.k9": MAIL_ICON,
    "eu.faircode.email": MAIL_ICON,
}
CATEGORY_ICONS = {"call": CALL_ICON, "email": MAIL_ICON, "event": CALENDAR_ICON, "reminder": CALENDAR_ICON}


def icon(package, category):
    return PACKAGE_ICONS.get(package) or CATEGORY_ICONS.get(category)


def worded(app, title, text, package=None, category=None):
    text = LEADING_TIME.sub("", text or "")
    if app == "ntfy":
        address = NTFY_ADDRESS.match(title or "")
        title = address.group(2) if address else title
        return NTFY_ICON + plain("{}: {}".format(title, text) if title else text)
    known = icon(package, category)
    if known:
        return known + plain("{}: {}".format(title or "", text))
    return plain("{}: {}: {}".format(app, title or "", text))


async def notify(peer, app, title, text, priority=3, when=None, package=None, category=None):
    await send_recall(peer, worded(app, title, text, package, category), priority, when)

the time is the one the story gives, written on TIME. 
async def send_time(peer, when):
    clock = peer.get_characteristics_by_uuid(TIME, SERVICE)[0]
    await peer.write_value(clock, struct.pack("<HBBBBBB", *when), with_response=True)
what
on the real air, until the android companion exists, this desktop stands in for the phone, through bleak over bluez.
  • why: bluez holds the desktop’s adapter; bleak speaks to it without root, where bumble would need it taken from bluez.
  • scope: it speaks the same protocol as the bumble companion, but bluez settles the packet size by itself.
import asyncio
import struct
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from bleak import BleakClient, BleakScanner

NAME = "twatch"
VOICE = "8d5a7819-0002-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01"
READY = "8d5a7819-0003-4b5a-a8f2-6f7a6c1b0e01"


async def receive_one(inbox):
    print("looking for the watch")
    watch = await BleakScanner.find_device_by_name(NAME, timeout=60)
    if watch is None:
        raise SystemExit("no watch seen in 60 s")
    async with BleakClient(watch) as client:
        print(f"linked to {watch.address}, packets of {client.mtu_size} bytes")
        received = bytearray()
        complete = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()

        def on_chunk(_, chunk):
            received.extend(chunk)
            if len(received) >= 4:
                (length,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", received)
                if len(received) - 4 >= length and not complete.done():
                    complete.set_result(bytes(received[4:4 + length]))

        await client.start_notify(VOICE, on_chunk)
        await client.write_gatt_char(READY, b"\x01", response=True)
        recording = await asyncio.wait_for(complete, 120)
    inbox.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = inbox / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S.wav")
    path.write_bytes(recording)
    print(f"saved {len(recording)} bytes in {path}")


asyncio.run(receive_one(Path(sys.argv[1])))
how
one command waits for one recording and saves it in the inbox it is given.

set -eu
